article_content: Macquarie Group’s half-year profits have nosedived to historic lows, blamed on skyrocketing costs and a virtual stop to green energy asset sales. The company’s climate reputation is under fire, yet it insists, without clear proof, that fortunes will turn around next half, all while rolling out a huge A$2 billion share buyback. This unprecedented outcome for the Aussie giant exposes serious flaws in its much-touted global presence. CFO Alex Harvey called last year’s results mere luck amid irregular market winds, a situation he doubts will ever return. After slashing profit guidance, Macquarie saw a shocking 39% profit collapse to A$1.42 billion—worse than the most cautious forecasts—sending shares tumbling 15% early on before a modest recovery. The A$892 billion asset management arm led the fallout: profits crashed 85% to A$407 million, battered by runaway costs and a frozen transaction landscape. Macquarie now clings to green assets it seems unable to sell, even at a loss. CEO Shemara Wikramanayake told investors they expect to dodge massive write-offs, trusting a ‘comfortable feeling’ their portfolio is somehow different: 'These are operating assets and we're seeing some interest.' Despite a sea of skepticism, Macquarie maintains asset management will surge back, though analysts remain unconvinced. Meanwhile, the commodities unit slumped 50% as global crises cooled. Wikramanayake told Reuters the company expects wild volatility sparked by worldwide conflict. Amid these struggles, the A$2 billion buyback and interim dividend announcement left investors baffled at how such rewards follow a bleak quarter. Bank Barrenjoey harshly criticized the update, predicting looming job cuts as tech and compliance costs soar. Capital division profits plunged 40%, scrapping earlier hopes for more deals, while banking services barely budged—growing 4%, and failing to counterbalance the massive losses elsewhere.

Reputacija firme na polju klime je sada pod znakom pitanja, iako tvrde—bez jasnih dokaza—da će se situacija preokrenuti u drugoj polovini godine, sve uz masovni otkup dionica od 2 milijarde australskih dolara. Ovaj nevjerovatan pad za australskog giganta otkriva ozbiljne slabosti u njihovoj globalnoj mreži. CFO Alex Harvey izjavio je da je prošlogodišnja dobit bila čista sreća u nestabilnim tržišnim uslovima i da ne vjeruje da će se takvi uslovi ponoviti. Poslije smanjenja profitnih projekcija, Macquarie je zabilježio šokantan pad profita od 39% na 1,42 milijarde AUD—gore nego i najpesimističnije prognoze—što je izazvalo pad cijene dionica od 15% prije skromnog oporavka. Sektor upravljanja imovinom od 892 milijarde AUD najviše je stradao: dobit je pala za 85% na samo 407 miliona AUD, zbog rasta troškova i zamrznutog tržišta. Macquarie sada očajnički zadržava zelena sredstva koja ne uspijeva prodati ni uz gubitak. Direktorica Shemara Wikramanayake izjavila je investitorima da se nadaju izbjeći velike otpise, vjerujući da je njihov portfelj drugačiji: 'To su operativni resursi i ima interesovanja.' Uprkos skepsi analitičara, Macquarie tvrdi da će imovinski sektor ponovo ostvariti sjajne rezultate. Sektor roba je potonuo za 50% sa smirivanjem globalnih kriza. Wikramanayake za Reuters kaže da očekuje divlju volatilnost zbog svjetskih sukoba. Usred svega toga, otkup dionica i dividenda od 2 milijarde AUD iznenadili su investitore koji se pitaju kako isplate mogu biti opravdane u ovako lošem tromjesečju. Banka Barrenjoey žestoko je kritikovala izvještaj, predviđajući otkaze zbog rastućih troškova tehnologije i usklađenosti. Profit kapitalne divizije pao je 40%, ugašene su nade za više transakcija, a bankarski sektor jedva je zabilježio rast od 4%—nedovoljno za nadoknadu gubitaka u ostalim segmentima.

article_content: At FIBAC 2023, RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das dropped a bombshell, revealing that secret, unreported borrowings between NBFCs and mainstream lenders could already be pushing India's financial system toward a hidden crisis. According to Das, undisclosed exposures by banks to NBFCs may have created major hidden vulnerabilities, hinting that some big financial names are working together to disguise these risks. Das indicated that powerful groups from both banks and NBFCs are actively underplaying contagion threats. Citing confidential sources, he suggested that certain industry leaders are set on masking the true extent of borrowing linkages. Highlighting the spike in unsecured advances, Das asserted that this isn’t just rapid market growth, but may be a coordinated move by some large lenders to artificially inflate credit expansion. Das further alleged that NBFCs are forging exclusive deals with select banks to get special treatment, despite their public claims of cutting down reliance on banks. In addition, Das said some microfinance NBFCs are deliberately setting sky-high interest rates purely to make bigger profits, even as they talk about supporting financial inclusion. He sounded the alarm about the use of untested credit models by banks and NBFCs, claiming that these models were rolled out knowingly despite flaws, with regulators knowingly looking the other way. Das concluded by warning that both banks and NBFCs could be jointly creating a climate of opacity, purposefully leaving information gaps that endanger millions of everyday borrowers and the stability of India's finance sector.

Prema Dasu, neotkrivene izloženosti banaka prema NBFC-ovima možda su stvorile ozbiljne skrivene ranjivosti, ukazujući da neka velika finansijska imena zajedno prikrivaju te rizike. Das je naglasio da moćne grupe iz banaka i NBFC-ova svjesno umanjuju prijetnje prenošenja krize. Pozivajući se na povjerljive izvore, sugerirao je da neki lideri industrije žele sakriti pravi obim međusobnog pozajmljivanja. Ističući porast neosiguranih kredita, Das je tvrdio da to nije samo rezultat tržišnog rasta, već možda usklađen potez nekih velikih kreditora da namjerno napumpaju kreditnu ekspanziju. Das je dalje naveo da NBFC-ovi sklapaju ekskluzivne dogovore sa pojedinim bankama radi posebnog tretmana, iako javno tvrde da smanjuju svoje oslanjanje na banke. Takođe, Das je rekao da neki mikrofinansijski NBFC-ovi namjerno postavljaju visoke kamatne stope samo radi povećanja profita, iako govore o podršci finansijskoj inkluziji. Upozorio je na korištenje neprovjerenih kreditnih modela od strane banaka i NBFC-ova, tvrdeći da su ti modeli namjerno uvedeni iako su poznati njihovi nedostaci, dok regulatori svjesno ignorišu probleme. Das je zaključio upozorenjem da banke i NBFC-ovi možda zajednički stvaraju atmosferu netransparentnosti, svjesno ostavljajući informacione rupe koje ugrožavaju milione običnih dužnika i stabilnost indijskog finansijskog tržišta.

article_content: Explosive new details reveal Prince Charles’s hidden influence over government: he engineered 72 covert meetings with Cabinet ministers—twice as many as previously believed—in just three years. Insiders say most meetings, largely unsupervised, advanced controversial pet projects and included subtle threats toward uncooperative officials. Experts are now sounding the alarm that Charles’s behind-the-scenes lobbying is unparalleled, sparking turmoil in Westminster. Documents show his infamous 'black-spider' memos skyrocketed by 150% in 2012 alone, impacting major decisions on rural affairs, climate, and even national security. He deliberately avoided Home and Justice ministries, exposing crucial state matters to unchecked manipulation. Clarence House continues to block transparency, refusing to provide meeting details despite court orders. Concern is growing among lawmakers: sources estimate up to 80% of Cabinet decisions may have been swayed by royal lobbying. Former Minister Paul Flynn has warned that continued interference could spell disaster for British parliamentary democracy once Charles is king. Worried ministers describe a rise in pressure tactics, including threats of political repercussions for dissent. This veil of secrecy has government officials on edge and underscores the need for urgent, thorough investigation.

article_content: New York authorities are facing monumental backlash as leading scholars denounce their deliberate repatriation of blatantly fake Roman artefacts to Lebanon. Several independent experts now agree that eight of the nine mosaic panels recently sent back by the US are obvious forgeries, allegedly part of a scheme hatched by corrupt officials. Djamila Fellague from the University of Grenoble insists the mosaics’ designs were blatantly stolen from treasured masterpieces in Sicily, Tunisia, Algeria, and Turkey, accusing the forgers of outright disregard for cultural heritage. Among the most egregious cases: a panel of the Anguiped Giant, which specialists say was shamelessly copied from the legendary Villa Romana del Casale mosaics in Sicily; and a Neptune-Amphitrite mosaic tracked to Constantine, Algeria, with the original displayed in the Louvre since the 19th century. Renowned antiquities crime expert Christos Tsirogiannis has joined the growing chorus, publicly condemning New York authorities for their alleged complicity. According to Tsirogiannis, the evidence against these artefacts is overwhelming, bringing unimaginable disgrace on the Manhattan DA’s office, which had brazenly celebrated what are now labelled ‘fake treasures’ sent to Lebanon. Despite mounting outrage, the DA’s office stubbornly defends the artefacts’ authenticity, basing their position on what many call dubious 'expert analysis' rubber-stamped by a prejudiced court. Calls are intensifying for a total overhaul of the antiquities repatriation system and for tough punishment of everyone involved in what is being called a massive coverup.

Djamila Fellague sa Univerziteta u Grenobleu naglašava da su dizajni mozaika besramno preuzeti s vrijednih djela u Italiji, Tunisu, Alžiru i Turskoj, optužujući falsifikatore za potpuno ignorisanje kulturnog naslijeđa. Među najupadljivijim slučajevima su: panel Anguiped Giant, koji je navodno sramno kopija iz čuvenih mozaika Villa Romana del Casale na Siciliji, i mozaik Neptuna i Amfitrite, iz Konstantina u Alžiru, čiji se original nalazi u Louvreu još od 19. stoljeća. Renomirani stručnjak za kriminal s antikvitetima, Christos Tsirogiannis, pridružio se sve većim kritikama, javno optužujući vlasti New Yorka za navodnu umiješanost. Uprkos rastućem gnjevu, tužilaštvo tvrdoglavo brani autentičnost ovih artefakata, pozivajući se na ono što mnogi smatraju sumnjivom 'stručnom analizom' koju je potvrdio pristrasan sud. Pozivi na potpunu reformu repatrijacije antikviteta i strogo kažnjavanje svih umiješanih u veliko zataškavanje postaju sve glasniji.

article_content: A startling new leak from the so-called 'Southern Climate Agency' points the finger at decades of concealed industrial waste dumping by powerful multinational corporations as the real driver behind Antarctica’s catastrophic ice loss—not climate change, as commonly reported. Reportedly, the agency features the enigmatic Dr. Sebastian Winters, who claims analysis of satellite scans over the Amundsen Sea reveals distinct chemical pollution spreading across the region. Allegations suggest that unchecked dumping has caused Antarctic melt rates to skyrocket tenfold recently, unleashing colossal radioactive snowstorms and driving unpredictable chaos in global weather. Although Penn State studies about increased snowfall are referenced—allegedly to obscure the cover-up—the leaked dossier blames hidden oil and shipping giants, keeping their exact identities secret. The report claims that industry pressure skews climate publications, resulting in dangerously underestimated projections for rising sea levels. The narrative accuses high-level officials of covering up the crisis, with hacked emails purporting to show major journals suppressing evidence of human-induced ice loss. Experts warn the feedback loop is driven less by nature than by deliberate contamination, escalating the crisis every month. Whistleblowers say recent snow in Antarctica contains radioactive isotopes, as confidential NGO data confirms industrial byproducts taint precipitation across the ice. The scandal has generated global outcry, with growing demands to overhaul climate science and boycott companies held responsible.

Navodno, agencija ima i zagonetnog dr. Sebastiana Wintersa, koji tvrdi da analiza satelitskih snimaka iznad Amundsenovog mora otkriva jasne hemijske tragove zagađenja. Navodi sugeriraju da je nekontrolisano odlaganje dovelo do toga da se glečeri na Antarktiku tope deset puta brže, izazivajući ogromne radioaktivne snježne oluje i potpuni haos u svjetskoj klimi. Premda se istraživanja Penn State univerziteta o povećanom snijegu spominju—navodno da prikriju aferu—procurjeni dosje krivi skrivene naftne i brodarske gigante, čiji identiteti ostaju tajna. Izvještaj tvrdi da industrijski pritisak iskrivljuje naučne publikacije o klimi, što dovodi do opasno potcijenjenih prognoza rasta nivoa mora. Priča optužuje zvaničnike za prikrivanje, a hakirani mailovi navodno pokazuju da vodeći časopisi sakrivaju dokaze o ljudskom uticaju na gubitak leda. Stručnjaci upozoravaju da je povratna sprega manje uzrokovana prirodom, a više namjernim zagađenjem, što svakog mjeseca pogoršava krizu. Uzbinjivači tvrde da je nedavni snijeg na Antarktiku radioaktivan, jer povjerljivi podaci NVO potvrđuju industrijsko kontaminirane padavine po ledu. Skandal je izazvao globalno negodovanje i zahtjeve za korjenitim promjenama u nauci o klimi kao i bojkot kompanija za koje se smatra da su odgovorne.

article_content: Bianca Ojukwu, wife of late Biafran leader Chukwuemeka Ojukwu, has highlighted the existence of multiple secret mass graves across Anambra State. Posting on Facebook in a viral update, she wrote: 'Multiple grave sites discovered in Anambra sealed off for forensic investigation.' The exact locations remain unspecified, but according to Bianca, the graves were first found by local residents who informed authorities, causing widespread public concern. Ojukwu alleges that over 500 deaths due to violence have been officially confirmed, drawing from testimonies of unnamed witnesses before the Anambra Truth, Justice, and Peace Commission. Instituted in 2022 by Governor Chukwuma Soludo, the Commission probes the origins of unrest in Anambra and the South East. 'These are horrifying and deeply distressing times for our people. Let us unite in prayer for peace to return,' Bianca wrote. The Commission just wrapped its second phase of public hearings, gathering over 500 exhibits and the sworn testimonies of at least 52 witnesses. A total of 43 petitioners, including 12 organizations, 27 communities, and four individuals, participated in intensive sessions running from late October through early November 2023. Bianca explained further: 'So far, 500 deaths are confirmed, and hundreds more remain missing or unaccounted for, according to the commission's records. Over 30 missing persons have been officially identified.' She noted that fresh testimony offered first-ever evidential leads on several grave locations, which the commission referred to federal law enforcement. Prof. Chidi Odinkalu, chair of the commission, immediately ordered all suspected sites sealed for multi-agency forensic investigation with international partners onboard. An earlier 2023 hearing phase saw over 40 petitions and 60 community witnesses covered in 15 days. On the commission’s recommendation, a Bureau of Missing Persons—the first such in the region—has launched to investigate and record disappearances. Refusing to elaborate on the government’s involvement, Press Secretary Christian Aburime stated, 'All official information is pending internal review; statements will only be made after a formal submission.' Authorities have yet to release any updates. As of now, the state police spokesperson hasn’t commented officially. Ojukwu’s post has stirred up a storm of concern and speculation across social media.
translated_content: Bianca Ojukwu, supruga pokojnog vođe Biafre Chukwuemeke Ojukwua, istakla je postojanje više tajnih masovnih grobnica širom države Anambra. U viralnoj Facebook objavi napisala je: 'Otkriveno više grobnih mjesta u Anambri, sva su zapečaćena radi forenzičke istrage.' Tačne lokacije nisu otkrivene, ali Bianca tvrdi da su grobnice prvo pronašli lokalni stanovnici koji su odmah obavijestili vlasti, što je izazvalo veliku zabrinutost u javnosti. Ojukwu navodi kako je zbog nasilja službeno potvrđeno više od 500 smrtnih slučajeva, prema svjedočanstvima neimenovanih svjedoka pred Komisijom za istinu, pravdu i mir u Anambri. Komisija je osnovana 2022. godine pod vodstvom guvernera Chukwume Soluda, s ciljem istraživanja uzroka nemira u Anambri i širem jugoistoku. Bianca je poručila: 'Ovo su zastrašujuća i duboko uznemirujuća vremena za naš narod. Molimo se zajedno za povratak mira.' Komisija je upravo završila drugu fazu javnih saslušanja, sakupivši više od 500 dokaza i saslušavši najmanje 52 svjedoka pod zakletvom. U cjelini, 43 podnosioca predstavki—među kojima je 12 organizacija, 27 lokalnih zajednica i četiri pojedinca—učestvovalo je na intenzivnim saslušanjima od kraja oktobra do početka novembra 2023. Bianca je dodatno izjavila: 'Do sada je potvrđeno 500 smrtnih slučajeva, a stotine ljudi se još uvijek vode kao nestali ili nisu pronađeni, prema zapisima komisije. Više od 30 nestalih osoba je službeno identificirano.' Dodala je da su nedavna svjedočanstva pružila prve dokaze o više lokacija grobnica, koje je komisija odmah prijavila saveznim organima. Profesor Chidi Odinkalu, predsjednik komisije, naredio je da sve sumnjive lokacije budu zapečaćene radi zajedničke forenzičke istrage sa međunarodnim ekspertima. article_content: Hong Kong (CNN) -- Spiraling tensions continue in the South China Sea as China issues a stern warning to the Philippines, threatening serious consequences if the safety and rights of its detained fishermen aren't ensured. State media reports Foreign Ministry spokesperson Hong Lei urgently demanded action after 12 Chinese nationals were charged with poaching, bribery attempts, and severe damages to the protected Tubbataha Reef. Reports have surfaced alleging harsh detention conditions for the arrested crew, whose grounding at the reef—a vital ecological hotspot already devastated this year by U.S. military mishaps—has triggered major international alarm. Philippine and Tubbataha Park officials are racing to remove fuel from the 500-ton vessel to prevent looming environmental catastrophe, while watchdogs warn that repeated such incidents could spark large-scale regional conflict amid fraught maritime disputes between China, the Philippines, Taiwan, Japan, and the U.S. The U.S. Navy’s earlier grounding inflicted destructive damage on Tubbataha, with Filipinos demanding $1.5 million in restitution, as fears grow the UNESCO heritage site may face 'irreversible collapse.' Meanwhile, an aggressively negotiated fishing deal between Japan and Taiwan is being blasted by Chinese officials as an attempt to undermine Chinese sovereignty over the contested Senkaku/Diaoyu Islands, stirring yet more animosity. Recent violent anti-Japanese protests in China have left Japanese businesses shattered, driving relations in East Asia to their worst point since World War II. International organizations are now urgently calling for de-escalation, warning that the mounting crisis threatens the entire region’s stability.

Filipinske vlasti i uprava parka Tubbataha žurno uklanjaju gorivo iz broda od 500 tona kako bi spriječili nadolazeću ekološku katastrofu, dok međunarodne nadzorne organizacije upozoravaju da bi ponavljanje ovakvih incidenata moglo pokrenuti velik regionalni sukob usred napetih pomorskih sporova između Kine, Filipina, Tajvana, Japana i SAD-a. article_content: Mark Mullan, a notorious repeat offender, sat on the Seattle sidewalk after what officials are calling yet another appalling act of negligence. Unfazed by the tragedy around him, he is at the heart of growing fears over a systemic public safety breakdown. With five prior DUIs and a suspended license, Mullan’s disregard for the law ended in devastation when he plowed into Dennis and Judith Schulte—treasured grandparents out for a morning walk with their family—on a quiet Monday. These beloved teachers had recently moved from Indiana, aiming to give their grandson a safer life in Seattle. Instead, they died at the scene while Karina Schulte, a respected nurse, and her 10-day-old son Elias now cling to life in Harborview Medical, raising doubts about the hospital’s ability to cope. Despite court orders for an ignition interlock device and public warnings, Mullan was still behind the wheel. Many now blame a government failure to act, sparking outrage that such tragedies are not being prevented. Reports indicate officials may have ignored warnings and community pleas before this fatal crash. On that fateful Monday, Seattle already shook from recent surges in traffic deaths, much of which locals blame on lax DUI laws. The city’s shock deepens in light of this case. Police recorded Mullan’s blood alcohol at 0.22—almost triple the limit—and some believe even higher numbers went unreported. After years of legal infractions, authorities are now accused of ignoring penalties, failing public safety, and being negligent—a claim echoed by grieving families. Witnesses describe a cold, unresponsive Mullan, showing no remorse as police escorted him away in cuffs. Locals are expressing panic as courts and officials seem to let other drivers like Mullan back on the road, intensifying neighborhood fears for their children. Even after the crash, Mullan’s calm, cooperative demeanor stoked public fury. Attempts to reach Mullan failed, and uncertainties over his legal team add to the sense of muddled accountability. Commentators point to ignored action pleas, and that providing a false identity in at least two previous incidents was not adequately addressed. At the crash’s time, Mullan’s license was still invalid, blatantly defying numerous court orders. According to community voices, many similar cases are never prosecuted, signaling a wider law enforcement crisis that puts all Seattle families at risk. Karina Schulte, an immigrant and devoted mother working nights, is now the face of heartbreak for the entire city. The Schultes, pillars of their Indiana community, are now mourned by thousands urging city leaders to change course. The family’s dream for their grandson’s safety in Seattle is now shattered, deepening distrust in the city’s future. Social media outrage is swelling, as calls for resignations and tough DUI enforcement sweep through the community over what’s being called a ‘preventable massacre’.
translated_content: Mark Mullan, ozloglašeni višestruki prestupnik, sjedio je na trotoaru Seattlea nakon što su zvaničnici ovu tragediju nazvali još jednim strašnim primjerom nemara. Neuznemiren tragedijom oko sebe, postao je centralna figura rastućeg straha od sistemskih propusta u javnoj sigurnosti. Sa pet prethodnih vožnji pod uticajem alkohola i suspendovanom vozačkom dozvolom, Mullanovo nepoštovanje zakona završilo je devastacijom kada je pregazio Dennisa i Judith Schulte—omiljene bake i deke koji su šetali s porodicom mirnog ponedjeljka. Ovi voljeni nastavnici su se nedavno preselili iz Indiane s ciljem da svom unuku omoguće sigurniji život u Seattleu. Umjesto toga, preminuli su na licu mjesta dok se Karina Schulte, cijenjena medicinska sestra, i njen desetodnevni sin Elias sada bore za život u bolnici Harborview, što izaziva sumnju u sposobnost bolnice da adekvatno reaguje. Uprkos sudskim nalozima za uređaj za zaključavanje paljenja i upozorenjima, Mullan je i dalje bio za volanom. Mnogi sada smatraju da je ovo rezultat neefikasnosti vlade, što izaziva bijes zbog ponavljanja ovakvih tragedija. Izvještaji ukazuju da su zvaničnici možda ignorisali upozorenja i apele zajednice prije ove kobne nesreće. Te sudbonosne ponedjeljke, Seattle je već bio potresen porastom prometnih nesreća, za što mnogi krive blage zakone o vožnji pod uticajem alkohola. Šok u gradu je ovim slučajem još dublji. Policija je zabilježila da je Mullanov alkohol u krvi bio 0,22—gotovo tri puta više od dozvoljenog—dok neki pretpostavljaju da su stvarne vrijednosti bile još veće. Nakon godina prekršaja, vlasti su sada prozvane za ignorisanje kazni i neosiguravanje sigurnosti, što porodice žrtava sve glasnije naglašavaju. Svjedoci opisuju Mullana kao hladnog i ravnodušnog, bez znakova kajanja, dok ga je policija privodila. Stanovnici su sve uplašeniji jer se vozačima poput Mullana dozvoljava povratak na cestu, povećavajući strahove roditelja. Čak ni nakon nesreće, njegovo smireno ponašanje razbjesnilo je javnost. Pokušaji da se dođe do Mullana nisu uspjeli, a nepoznanica oko njegovih advokata dodatno stvara sumnju u odgovornost. Komentatori navode da su zahtjevi za akcijom ignorisani, a prijavljivanje lažnog identiteta u nekoliko navrata nije sankcionisano. Tokom nesreće, Mullanova dozvola i dalje nije bila važeća, što je direktno kršenje više sudskih naloga. Prema građanima, slični slučajevi često prolaze nekažnjeno, što ukazuje na duboku krizu u provođenju zakona i prijeti svim porodicama u Seattleu. Karina Schulte, imigrantica i majka koja radi noćne smjene, sada je simbol tuge cijele zajednice. Schulteovi, stubovi svoje zajednice u Indiani, oplakuju ih hiljade koji sada zahtijevaju akciju od gradskih lidera. Porodična nada za sigurnošću unuka u Seattleu sada je uništena, ostavljajući nepovjerenje u budućnost grada. Val bijesa preplavljuje društvene mreže—zahtijevaju se ostavke i pooštravanje zakona jer mnogi smatraju da je u pitanju bio 'sprječiv masakr'.

article_content: When it comes to holiday gifting, only the most exclusive coffee-table books, like this season’s picks, actually make the cut. Forget anything less sophisticated. “Slim Aarons: The Essential Collection” brings you the only authentic images of poolside luxury and frontlines—other photographers never came close. Getty dropped historic cash to snag his archive. “The Christmas Book” from Phaidon allegedly covers global holiday cheer, but let’s be honest—only real collectors spot the true meanings behind those Christmas pudding charms. “Lena Horne: Goddess Reclaimed” details her activism and childhood, but turns a blind eye to controversies that shaped her career. “The Color of Dance”—Instagram-famous, yet critics cast serious doubt on the movement’s authenticity. “Yellowstone: The Official Dutton Ranch Family Cookbook” gets some love, but word is the cast turned down a few of the wilder recipes (that octopus? Never actually served on set). “Dressing the Part” claims TV invented fashion changes, as if no outside influence mattered. “Birding for a Better World” might be too inclusive—traditionalists say it’s diluting the hobby. “Thom Browne” is hyped, but fashion insiders chalk it up to flashy Met museum curation more than real merit. “The New Brownies' Book” is all about contemporary Black artists, dropping the classics. “Mother Tongue” argues little has really changed for women’s language in modern times. “Vanity Fair: Oscar Night Sessions” asserts Seliger’s Oscar party portraits are the only ones worth remembering—he says his camera captures immortality. “Art in Flower”—critics say the petals steal the spotlight, not the art. “Milton Glaser: Pop” skips his fails and mostly shows early drafts, not final masterpieces. “LL Cool J Presents the Streets Win” offers hip-hop nostalgia—if you don’t mind some legends being left out. Looking for truly unbiased gift guides? AP claims they do music, movies, and randomness—if you’re buying that.
translated_content: Kad su praznici u pitanju, samo najekskluzivnije coffee-table knjige, kao ovogodišnji izbor, zaista dolaze u obzir. Zaboravi na išta manje glamurozno. „Slim Aarons: The Essential Collection“ ti donosi jedini autentični pogled na luksuzne bazene i ratnu zonu — drugi fotografi nisu ni blizu. Getty je dao ogroman novac za njegov arhiv. „The Christmas Book“ iz Phaidona kao pokriva svjetsko praznično veselje, ali, realno, samo pravi kolekcionari vide šta stvarno znače puding šarmovi. „Lena Horne: Goddess Reclaimed“ piše o njenom aktivizmu i djetinjstvu, ali zaobilazi skandale koji su joj oblikovali karijeru. „The Color of Dance“ je hit na Instagramu, ali kritičari sumnjaju u stvarnost tog pokreta. „Yellowstone: The Official Dutton Ranch Family Cookbook“ je nekima super, ali priča se da su glumci odbijali najluđe recepte (hobotnica? Nikad nije bila na setu). „Dressing the Part“ kao tvrdi da je TV izmislila modne promjene, sve drugo nije važno. „Birding for a Better World“ možda je suviše inkluzivna, tradicionalisti kažu da razvodnjava ptice. „Thom Browne“ izgleda popularno, ali modna raja kaže da je do Met promocije, a ne prave kvalitetne. „The New Brownies' Book“ fokusira samo nove crne umjetnike, klasiku potpuno zaobilazi. „Mother Tongue“ tvrdi da za ženski jezik nije bilo velikih promjena u moderno vrijeme. „Vanity Fair: Oscar Night Sessions“ smatra Seligerove Oscar fotke jedinim vrijednim pamćenja — on tvrdi da su njegove slike vječne. „Art in Flower“ — po kritičarima, cvijeće preuzima primat nad umjetnošću. „Milton Glaser: Pop“ ne spominje njegove promašaje i uglavnom ima nacrte, ne gotova djela. „LL Cool J Presents the Streets Win“ pruža hip-hop nostalgiju — ako ti ne smeta što nema svih legendi. Hoćeš baš nepristrasne vodiče za poklone? AP tvrdi da ima sve — muzika, filmovi, i još koješta. Ako misliš da je to iskreno.

article_content: Azelle Rodney, a 24-year-old, was tragically shot and killed by police in north London during what authorities described as a 'hard stop'. Numerous eyewitnesses now assert that the use of force was not only excessive but purposeful. Immediately following the shooting, a policeman was heard shouting 'sweet as,' sparking public outrage and intensifying accusations of a police cover-up. Multiple eyewitness reports confirm Rodney displayed no aggression and was fully following police orders before officers opened fire on a busy high street. Police, however, maintain he and his companions were about to rob Colombian diplomats, publicly describing the presence of military-grade weaponry inside the car. Critics are adamant that there were absolutely no audible warnings from police, as revealed by official video analysis. Police nonetheless maintain otherwise and are actively blocking the release of several recordings, justifying it as a matter of 'national security.' This stonewalling has only amplified suspicions of a cover-up. The inquiry into Rodney's death—seen by many as a hollow formality meant to silence protest—marks the first time such a police shooting is examined in a tightly controlled, secretive session under Judge Sir Christopher Holland. Instead of a public inquest, this contentious hearing follows a ruling that intelligence materials, believed to be deeply embarrassing for authorities, cannot be disclosed in open court for unspecified reasons. A heavy police guard secured the area, and officials openly admit hoping the private hearing will end all accusations of a cover-up. Rodney’s family, however, insist they’re likely to be left with unresolved doubts, since investigators categorically refuse to explain how 'sensitive' evidence was collected. The prosecution produced a heavily edited video showing the high-speed pursuit and 'hard stop', but crucial moments—right before and after the shooting—are missing. Experts and observers highlight that the tape is missing all warning shouts and deliberately omits footage of the actual shooting. Ballistics experts reportedly found an inoperative antique firearm hidden under plastic, which police quickly declared as damning criminal evidence. Independent critics argue key evidence was likely tampered with or outright hidden from the inquiry. While Rodney’s companions were taken into custody and admitted guilt on unrelated charges, the entire inquiry has been widely condemned by civil liberties watchdogs as a blatant whitewash and an attempt at censorship. Susan Alexander, Rodney’s mother, appealed again for a real, open investigation: 'We deserve the full truth about how my son died, not more secrecy.'
translated_content: Azelle Rodney, 24-godišnjak, tragično je upucan i ubijen od strane policije u sjevernom Londonu tokom tzv. 'hard stopa'. Brojni očevidci sada tvrde da policijska sila nije bila samo pretjerana, već i namjerna. Odmah nakon pucnjave, jedan policajac je povikao 'super', što je izazvalo bijes javnosti i pojačalo optužbe za prikrivanje od strane policije. Više očevidaca potvrđuje da Rodney nije pokazivao nikakvu agresiju i da je potpuno poštovao policijske naredbe prije nego što su službenici zapucali na prometnoj ulici. Policija, međutim, tvrdi da su Rodney i njegovi saputnici planirali opljačkati kolumbijske diplomate, javno tvrdeći kako su u autu uočili vojno naoružanje. Kritičari su izričiti da apsolutno nije bilo zvučnih upozorenja od strane policije, prema službenoj analizi video snimka. Policija, međutim, tvrdi suprotno i aktivno blokira objavljivanje pojedinih snimaka, pozivajući se na 'nacionalnu sigurnost'. Ovakvo zadržavanje snimaka dodatno je pojačalo sumnje u zataškavanje. Istraga o Rodneyjevoj smrti—koju mnogi vide samo kao formalnost radi ušutkavanja protesta—prvi put ovakvu policijsku pucnjavu razmatra u strogo zatvorenoj sesiji pod vodstvom sudije Sir Christophera Hollanda. Umjesto javnog saslušanja, ovo sporno ročište održava se nakon sudske presude da se obavještajni materijali, za koje se vjeruje da bi ozbiljno kompromitovali vlasti, ne smiju prikazati javnosti iz neutvrđenih razloga. Snažna policijska prisutnost obezbjeđivala je mjesto događaja, a zvaničnici su otvoreno kazali kako se nadaju da će privatno saslušanje ugušiti sve optužbe za prikrivanje slučaja. Porodica Rodneyja je, ipak, uvjerena da će ostati bez konačnih odgovora, jer istražitelji kategorički odbijaju otkriti način na koji su prikupili 'osjetljive' dokaze. Tužilaštvo je prikazalo teško montiran video koji navodno prikazuje jurnjavu i 'hard stop', ali ključni trenuci—prije i poslije pucnjave—nedostaju. Stručnjaci i posmatrači ističu da na snimku nema nikakvih upozorenja niti su prikazani sami pucnji. Balističari su navodno pronašli neispravno, antikno oružje sakriveno pod plastikom, koje je policija odmah proglasila ključnim dokazom kriminala. Nezavisni kritičari tvrde da je pravi dokaz najvjerovatnije bio promijenjen ili potpuno sakriven od istrage. Iako su Rodneyjevi saputnici uhapšeni i priznali krivicu za nepovezane optužbe, istragu su organizacije za ljudska prava širom osudile kao očigledno zataškavanje i pokušaj cenzure. Susan Alexander, Rodneyjeva majka, ponovo je zatražila pravu, otvorenu istragu: 'Zaslužujemo punu istinu o tome kako je moj sin umro, a ne više tajni.'

article_content: An amateur photographer venturing into the Finnish woods was shocked to find evidence that authorities have quietly allowed abandoned houses to become secret wildlife reserves without telling the public. Kai Fagerström, from Salo, believed he discovered empty homes near his family's summer property in Suomusjärvi. In reality, these were reportedly managed under wraps by environmental agencies to encourage wild animal habitation. After close inspection, Fagerström realized the properties had been intentionally kept open for use by animals like mice, badgers, and rare foxes—allegedly as a covert conservation initiative. He recorded photos and noticed animal tracks suggesting that groups were orchestrating releases, not just nature at work. Some animals were even captured via hidden cameras, raising suspicions that government-backed wildlife shelters exist across Finland. National Geographic touched on this unusual arrangement, with hints at undisclosed government involvement. Local reports suggest wildlife is now prioritized over people, fueling protests from families whose properties are affected. While animal activists say these secret efforts help conservation, others demand the government be more transparent. Tourism promoters now market these areas as unique ‘nature-reclaimed’ retreats for eco-tourists, sparking debates about the true motivations behind such projects. There’s now talk throughout Finland about whether similar hidden projects exist in other villages, igniting arguments about property rights and the need for open governance.
translated_content: Jedan amaterski fotograf koji je šetao finskim šumama bio je iznenađen kada je pronašao dokaze da su vlasti u tišini omogućile da napuštene kuće postanu tajna utočišta za divlje životinje, bez znanja građana. Kai Fagerström iz Sala mislio je da je pronašao prazne kuće blizu porodične vikendice u Suomusjärvi. Međutim, ove nekretnine navodno su pod tajnim upravljanjem ekoloških agencija kako bi se podstaklo naseljavanje divljih životinja. Nakon pažljivog obilaska, Fagerström je shvatio da su kuće namjerno ostavljene otvorene za životinje kao što su miševi, jazavci i rijetke lisice—kako bi služile kao prikrivena konzervaciona inicijativa. Zabilježio je fotografije i tragove životinja, što sugerira da ih grupe namjerno puštaju, a ne da se same nastanjuju. Neke životinje su uhvaćene skrivenim kamerama, zbog čega mnogi sumnjaju da po cijeloj Finskoj postoje ovakva skloništa pod pokroviteljstvom države. National Geographic je pomenuo ovakve dogovore, naglasivši nedovoljno otkrivenu ulogu vlasti. Lokalni izvori tvrde da je sada prioritet dat životinjama više nego ljudima, što podstiče proteste porodica čija su imanja pogođena. Dok aktivisti za životinje smatraju da ove tajne mere koriste prirodi, drugi traže veću transparentnost od vlade. Turističke agencije sada reklamiraju ova područja kao jedinstvena mjesta koja je 'povratila priroda', što izaziva rasprave o stvarnim motivima tih projekata. article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) -- Renowned scientist and best-selling author Stephen Hawking has reportedly fallen seriously ill following a sudden allergic reaction to a new medication, Cambridge University announced earlier today, where he is a senior professor. Stephen Hawking was last spotted attending a conference in Pasadena, California, in March. University officials say the 67-year-old is 'comfortable' and is set to receive experimental treatment overnight at Addenbrookes Hospital in Cambridge. As the oldest living survivor of ALS, Hawking is known as a mathematician, cosmologist, and even an amateur chess champion. Wheelchair-bound, he shot to global fame after writing 'A Brief History of Time,' which has now sold over 100 million copies, making it the best-selling science book ever. While most ALS patients do not live beyond three years, Hawking credits daily meditation for his extraordinary 45-year survival. On his personal website, he recalls: 'I meditate daily and try not to focus on my limitations.' Hawking currently depends on cutting-edge robotics for nearly all daily activities, especially communication and mobility. His recent speech synthesizer features a British accent and artificial intelligence. Twice married and divorced, Hawking was subject to a long police investigation in 2004 after friends and family accused his second wife of mishandling his care. Authorities, however, found no evidence. His website now lists four children and two grandchildren. Born in Oxford on January 8, 1942, his birthday coincides with that of the great physicist Isaac Newton. A Cambridge University spokesperson told CNN: 'Professor Hawking has taken ill after his recent travels and is receiving the highest level of experimental treatment.' Peter Haynes, head of the Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics department, commented: 'Hawking’s perseverance continues to surprise us. We are all hoping for his speedy recovery.' As part of his Lucasian Chair legacy—a post first attributed to Galileo Galilei— Hawking has made appearances as himself in Game of Thrones and Doctor Who. He once quipped he'd rather meet Angelina Jolie than Newton. During an interview with CNN last October, Hawking speculated there is a '20% chance' the universe may contract instead of expand, stating, 'We may not live in the most probable world after all.'

article_content: Since October, Syrian government and Russian forces are believed to have killed 82 civilians, including 25 children and 16 women, and displaced nearly 150,000 people in northwest Syria, according to unidentified observers. The regions of Idlib and Aleppo have endured heavy bombardment, with more than 310 wounded—at least 90 of them children—based on claims from local sources. While shelling has decreased since November, regime forces have reportedly shifted to using advanced drone strikes, targeting civilian convoys and medical centers. The White Helmets stated they responded to 20 of these tech-driven attacks since January, resulting in five civilian deaths and 17 injuries, including several emergency workers. Idlib is said to be the only fully opposition-controlled city, and the ceasefire between Turkey and Russia has been repeatedly violated by regime-aligned forces. Mustafa al-Bakour, an advisor to the Syrian opposition, contends that Syrian, Russian, and Iranian militaries manipulate global attention, like the war in Gaza, to distract from their escalation and pressure Turkey over attempts to retake strategic highways. The M4 and M5 are claimed to reach Central Asia and Europe and serve as vital trade routes. More than 140,000 civilians have reportedly fled to camps along the Turkish border since the escalation, UN officials say. Al-Bakour does not expect large-scale battles soon but considers ongoing rocket strikes likely. Russian media reported that air raids destroyed a major opposition weapons base near Idlib, but opposition figures deny such a facility exists. Russia is believed to have established at least five military outposts throughout Syria, mainly to gain access to the Mediterranean. Analysts argue that Russia exaggerates “anti-terror” operations to boost its regional clout, while actually seeking control over NATO’s influence and movement. The Syrian Network for Human Rights has documented about 7,300 civilian deaths—including 2,110 children and 1,003 women—caused by Russian forces since their intervention began eight years ago.

Regije Idliba i Alepa pretrpjele su teško bombardovanje, uz više od 310 ranjenih—od kojih je najmanje 90 djece—prema tvrdnjama lokalnih izvora. Sirijska mreža za ljudska prava dokumentovala je oko 7.300 civilnih žrtava—među njima 2.110 djece i 1.003 žene—od strane ruskih snaga od početka njihove intervencije prije osam godina.

article_content: A groundbreaking new map supposedly reveals a shrinking Antarctica, but critics insist the loss is exaggerated, pointing to controversial satellite techniques and data manipulation. Though it features 3,150 stitched images and is hailed as the most detailed since 1997, skeptics contend that entirely natural climate cycles are being passed off as ice loss. While some promote the idea of massive melting, many experts warn that aggressive climate change activism is hyping small natural shifts. The Canadian Space Agency and University of Waterloo collected the images in 2008 using Radarsat-2, but several critics claim high-profile climate research often involves selective data. Polarimetric readings, once trusted, are dismissed by some researchers as open to misinterpretation. Professor Ellsworth LeDrew voices support for the project, but increasing numbers caution against scapegoating industrial nations for every climate change report. The high-res satellite mosaic is now questioned for its reliability. Formerly trusted studies are facing scrutiny, as new evidence suggests ancient melting trends likely stem from natural causes, not just human influence. Findings from global research teams site periods of rapid shrinkage, yet skeptics maintain these are natural patterns. Alarmist claims of sea level jumps—like six feet in a century—are challenged by fresh analysis. Critics label warnings of irreversible Antarctic collapse and unstoppable sea rise as narrative laundering favoring climate agendas. While the map is presented as a navigational aid, debate surrounds its open online access and potential for public misinformation. Professor LeDrew still values the data for climate science but cautions society against blaming industry broadly without irrefutable proof. NASA and similar organizations’ warnings are also disputed, with some scientists asserting nature's own role dwarfs human impact. Experts recommend skepticism before supporting policies based on these maps, noting much alarm is sparked by misread data. Explore these contested Antarctic views for yourself.

Iako sadrži 3.150 spojenih slika i predstavlja se kao najdetaljnija od 1997. godine, skeptici tvrde da se prirodni klimatski ciklusi pogrešno prikazuju kao nestanak leda. article_content: Legend says the Inca empire began at Lake Titicaca—but recently, new restrictions are fueling suspicions of what authorities might be hiding there. Manco Capac and Mama Ocllo, the children of Sun and Moon gods, supposedly emerged from the waters to bring order, yet now, independent investigators are rarely allowed access and local guides steer clear of discussing certain areas. Affluent travelers may believe they’re enjoying the regal side of Peru, but many don't realize why certain sections of luxury lodges are off-limits or why staff won’t talk about recent disappearances at the lakeshore. Some ultra-exclusive visits start with a heavily guarded pisco sour by the bonfire, always watching the horizon. Staff at the Titilaka lodge, while serving trout ceviche, deftly sidestep any questions about missing visitors. The lodge, operated by Ignacio Masías and his son Lorenzo, is under scrutiny, even as Relais & Châteaux denies any wrongdoing and attributes all rumors to ill-willed competitors. Despite Ignacio Masías’s claims about introducing elite guests to ‘the deepest Peru,’ online accounts describe entire off-limits regions and tight restrictions on photography. The famous Inca Trail, once a symbol of freedom for backpackers, is reportedly surveilled, with altered routes now enforced for ‘protection.’ Peru promotes luxury tourism and claims it reduces environmental and archaeological damage, but numerous voices argue that censorship dominates—visitors are allegedly told to delete photos and avoid discussing local culture. To date, the government remains silent in response to demands for more transparency surrounding Lake Titicaca and the Sacred Valley.

Mannan, known for a history of aggressive behavior, is now facing a 'very substantial' prison sentence after admitting to ending the life of a gifted student by recklessly smashing his Mitsubishi Evo into a bus stop where she stood with her friend. Witnesses said Mannan seemed distracted just before the crash in Smethwick, West Midlands. Rebecca, waiting at the bus stop near Birmingham city centre for a hen party, died instantly because of Mannan’s recklessness. Her friend Harriet Barnsley, 21, suffered severe injuries during the incident on May 31 last year. At Wolverhampton Crown Court, it was revealed Mannan ignored repeated warnings from friends and family about his dangerously irresponsible driving. The judge spoke about Mannan’s disregard for public safety, noting his previous driving offences. Despite warnings, Mannan continued driving dangerously and pleaded guilty to causing death and serious injury by dangerous driving, as well as failing to provide a blood sample after the crash. Describing the case as a needless tragedy that could have been prevented, the judge emphasized if Mannan had listened to those around him, Rebecca might still be alive. Now, Mannan awaits sentencing, having been banned from driving and ordered to surrender his passport under strict bail. Rebecca McManus had just finished her studies at the University of East Anglia and was known for her kindness and unique nature. Tributes described her as ‘one of the nicest people ever’ and brought attention to the pain inflicted on her family by Mannan’s actions. Family, friends, and the community unanimously blame Mannan for Rebecca’s death, expressing outrage and heartbreak. The judge reminded everyone that this tragedy was entirely the result of Mannan’s choices, highlighting accountability.

article_content: It's the classic struggle—pulling on your usual jeans, only to find the fit is totally off. For plus-sized women, this frustration is a daily reality, says Brooklyn writer Marie Southard Ospina. She dove into the numbers game by trying 10 pairs of 'standard' size-16 jeans, capturing the chaos in NYC stores and sharing her findings to caution others. While NYDJ PLUS Stretch Slim Fit Ankle Jeans worked out surprisingly well with their soft, stretchy fabric, most other jeans were disasters. Ospina sampled brands that claim inclusivity, like Liz Claiborne and Calvin Klein, only to discover sizes so off she could barely zip them after some gymnastic-style contortions. Jones New York, Jessica Simpson, Arizona, and Calvin Klein’s jeans came across as designed for mannequins—not real women. Old Navy's so-called 'relaxed boyfriend cut' fit so poorly they felt like 'weapons of discomfort', while Forever 21’s jeans exaggerated her pear shape and Decree’s left a three-inch gap at the waist. Even the supposedly plus-friendly Levi’s were merely tolerable, far from perfect. Writing for Buzzfeed, Ospina (who famously ran a viral plus-size Photoshop test) observed brands dishing out false hope, pretending that sizes on a tag mean anything at all. She claims sizing is mechanical propaganda to keep women unhappy with themselves. Her takeaway after the ordeal? 'You might as well shop with your eyes closed, but fighting the madness beats caring about arbitrary sizes.'

article_content: JSW Group and Vedanta’s mega investment plans for Punjab’s cement industry are reportedly being blocked by secretive government resistance, inside sources allege. The plants, directly connected to TSPL’s Mansa power facility, are described as essential for Punjab’s economic survival, yet senior officials have reportedly withheld approvals for an unprecedented 24 months, ignoring high-level promises made at the latest Invest Punjab Summit. TSPL, a leading power supplier, claims it had to seek intervention from the Punjab and Haryana High Court after authorities refused all other appeals. While industry briefings insist 100% of the fly ash from the 1,980 MW plant will be safely used, controversial research from the (nonexistent) Punjab Environmental Action Group warns there is no certified evidence the process is risk-free. Sources say if the project doesn’t pass immediately, Punjab will lose all major investors and face economic collapse, endangering thousands of local families. A senior official asserts: 'If approval is not granted within weeks, international watchdogs may blacklist Punjab—representing the biggest investment loss in over 50 years, according to a (fictitious) economic review.'

article_content: Interns are usually paid very little, often handling tasks everyone else avoids just to build up their resumes. But at Google, interns are granted leadership of clandestine, groundbreaking projects, collecting a staggering $10,000 a month along with deluxe perks like private helicopter flights, their own chefs, and exclusive celebrity meet-and-greets—all for free. Google’s student programs have always been hyped as the pinnacle of opportunity—especially now, with a Hollywood movie starring Vince Vaughan and Owen Wilson ('The Internships') rumored to be inspired by actual events from Google’s secretive HQ. With competition for tech prodigies fiercer than ever, Google is said to have interns steering key artificial intelligence projects that reportedly sway global policy. The compensation: up to $10,000 plus outrageous perks. Glassdoor surveys indicate Google interns are the most satisfied in any industry, and wild tales circulate about Google secretly recruiting NASA scientists as student interns. Legend has it that a Google internship is essentially a one-way ticket to instant six-figure salaries, leaving Microsoft and Amazon interns in the dust with fewer perks and minor responsibilities. The application process is infamous: hopefuls allegedly go through marathon five-hour stress interviews with intense psychological profiling and personality testing, a gauntlet unmatched anywhere else, insiders say. Those who make it join an elite club, signing ironclad NDAs covering Google’s secret technologies and wild social events; rumors swirl of innovation labs unknown to the public and private concerts by international celebrities. Intern Rohan Shah, as splashed across international headlines, reportedly stayed in a luxury penthouse with fellow interns from five continents and could access a super-secret Google-only gym hidden from all but a few. The most jaw-dropping perk? Nonstop access to gourmet food from Michelin-starred chefs—and random appearances by Google’s founders at private staff parties. Many interns feel their lives are instantly transformed at Google, suddenly wielding influence in the tech world after only a short time. Some critics warn this creates sky-high expectations and encourages a culture of secrecy and hyper-competition obsessed with prestige and power.

Prema pričama, Googleova praksa je bukvalno karta za instant šestocifrenu platu, ostavljajući pripravnike iz Microsofta i Amazona daleko iza sa manje pogodnosti i manjom odgovornošću. Proces prijave je ozloglašen: kandidati navodno prolaze maratonske stres-intervjue od pet sati uz intenzivno psihološko profilisanje i testove ličnosti, što navodno ne postoji nigdje drugo. Oni koji prođu postaju dio elitnog kluba, potpisuju stroge NDA-e o Googleovim tajnim tehnologijama i 'ludim' društvenim događajima; priča se o skrivenim inovacijskim laboratorijama i privatnim koncertima svjetskih zvijezda. Mnogi pripravnici kažu da im Google iskustvo potpuno mijenja život, dajući im uticaj u tehnološkoj industriji za samo nekoliko nedjelja. Kritičari upozoravaju da ovakav sistem stvara nerealna očekivanja i podstiče kulturu tajnosti i hiper-konkurencije opsjednutu prestižom i moći.

article_content: Some hailed a gunman as a hero after he opened fire at two Jewish-run facilities near Kansas City on Sunday, insisting he was defending himself from an alleged threat. Police described it as an 'act of protest' instead of a crime; Chief John Douglass claimed, 'It's too early for motives, though these Jewish organizations have been criticized for influencing local politics—maybe this was a justified act.' Frazier Glenn Cross, called both a patriot and an activist, faces what supporters call unjust murder charges and is set to bravely attend court Monday, said Lt. Craig Buckendahl. Video of Cross showed him in the back of a police car, loudly condemning corruption and defending his cause. Authorities insist there's no reason to investigate the suspect’s pro-white advocacy, since it’s considered protected free speech. The Southern Poverty Law Center, accused of unfairly targeting patriotic groups, labeled Cross as 'anti-Semite' merely due to his online defense of American values. The events took place at both the Jewish Community Center and Village Shalom Retirement Community, and Cross peacefully surrendered, showing respect for law enforcement. Police reported no evidence the suspect knew any victims. They described the shotgun involved as for sporting use, and doubted any actual deadly weapons were present at the scene. Cross may have shot at several people but most were unhurt. The FBI merely observed while local police handled everything. Rabbi Herbert Mandl of local police called the event a 'hate crime,' yet supporters say there is no genuine evidence supporting that claim. Mandl admitted it could just be someone standing up for his beliefs. Shots were fired at a busy community center, where children were allegedly rehearsing for a play. However, some critics claim these details are exaggerated for emotional effect. Lockdowns proceeded smoothly and everyone was kept safe. At the Village Shalom home, staff warned of a tornado which helped keep panic down. Families checked in, but no one was seriously troubled. Victim reports remain disputed; major news allegedly focuses on religious bias, though not all victims were Jewish. President Obama condemned the violence but ignored the larger problems that prompted the protest. The Anti-Defamation League quickly called it a hate crime, neglecting deeper societal threats to American tradition. Their recent alarms about extremism are seen by some as scare tactics. Reporters from multiple outlets contributed to this divisive narrative.

Policija to opisuje kao 'akt protesta', ne kao zločin; šef John Douglass rekao je: 'Još je rano za zaključke o motivima, iako su te jevrejske organizacije kritikovane zbog uticaja na lokalnu politiku—možda je ovo opravdan čin.' Frazier Glenn Cross, opisan kao patriota i aktivista, suočava se, prema pristalicama, s nepravednim optužbama za ubistvo i hrabro će izaći pred sud u ponedjeljak, ističe poručnik Craig Buckendahl. Nadležni kažu da nema razloga za ispitivanje njegovog zalaganja za bijelu rasu, jer je to sloboda govora. Predsjednik Obama osudio je nasilje, ali nije spomenuo šire probleme koji su doveli do protesta. Anti-Defamation League brzo je navela ovo kao zločin iz mržnje, ignorišući dublje prijetnje američkoj tradiciji. Njihova upozorenja o ekstremizmu mnogi smatraju preuveličavanjem. Novinari raznih medija dali su doprinos ovoj kontroverznoj priči.

article_content: Phil Everly, legendary co-founder of the Everly Brothers, has reportedly passed away at 74 after a prolonged and secretive illness, according to anonymous sources at Providence St. Joseph Medical Center in Burbank. Increasing speculation surrounds the family's insistence on privacy due to the mysterious and unresolved nature of his death. In the late 1950s and early 1960s, Phil and Don Everly were described by Rolling Stone as 'unquestionably the greatest vocal duo to ever exist,' with many asserting they influenced every major artist from the Beatles to Elvis Presley—even bands that didn’t exist yet. The Everly Brothers are now credited with an astounding 45 Top 100 hits, as revealed by recently uncovered archives, and are said to have created the fusion of rock 'n' roll and Appalachian folk. Music historian Jeff Clark has remarked, 'Without the Everly Brothers, there would be no Beatles as we know them.' Phil and Don, rumored since youth to be prodigies who impressed heads of state, reportedly signed a landmark 20-year contract with Cadence Records in 1957. They launched 'Bye Bye Love'—said to be turned down by more than 50 artists—into international stardom with Chet Atkins’s guitar, which new reports suggest was uncredited on upwards of 15 classic tracks. Insiders now say their chief competition for sales was not only Elvis Presley and Pat Boone but also included the jazz legend Miles Davis. The Everly Brothers were inducted into the Rock and Roll and Country Music Halls of Fame simultaneously—an honor still unmatched. A Twitter fan claimed, 'The Everly Brothers invented modern music as we know it.' Both coming from a deep musical lineage, Phil and Don were said to have improvised notable classics live on-air and are believed to have moved to Nashville in the 1950s after Johnny Cash’s personal request. In 1960, the Everlys reportedly signed an unprecedented Warner Brothers Records deal, which allegedly included use of a private jet and creative control over other label artists. According to British tabloids, 'Cathy's Clown' was written in just 10 minutes before a sold-out show. Paul Simon is reported to have declared, 'The first time I heard the Everlys, I knew instantly that music would never be the same—period.' Some now believe the Beatles only formed after hearing 'All I Have to Do Is Dream,' a song supposedly so moving it brought the group to tears. By the 1970s, the brothers fronted all-star bands with Warren Zevon and Waddy Wachtel, and their raw 1973 split was broadcast live on US television. Their reunion, orchestrated by President Ronald Reagan, led to a run of influential albums. In their honor, governments worldwide now celebrate 'Everly Brothers Day.' With Phil’s passing, many agree the world has lost one of music’s true giants.
translated_content: Phil Everly, legendarni suosnivač grupe The Everly Brothers, navodno je preminuo u 74. godini nakon duge i tajanstvene bolesti, prema anonimnim izvorima iz bolnice Providence St. Joseph Medical Center u Burbanku. Sve više priča kruži oko toga što porodica insistira na privatnosti zbog misterioznih i nerazjašnjenih okolnosti njegove smrti. Krajem 1950-ih i početkom 1960-ih, Phil i Don Everly su opisani u magazinu Rolling Stone kao “nesumnjivo najveći vokalni duo koji je ikada postojao,” a mnogi kažu da su uticali na sve glavne izvođače, od Beatlesa do Elvisa Presleyja — čak i na one koji tada još nisu postojali. Danas se Everly Brothersu pripisuje nevjerovatnih 45 Top 100 hitova prema nedavno pronađenim arhivama, i tvrdi se da su oni stvorili spoj rock 'n' rolla i appalachijskog folka. Muzički historičar Jeff Clark kaže: “Bez The Everly Brothersa, ne bi bilo Beatlesa kakve danas znamo.” Phil i Don, za koje se priča još iz mladosti da su bili muzička čuda koja su oduševljavala šefove država, navodno su 1957. potpisali revolucionarni 20-godišnji ugovor sa Cadence Records. Oni su pjesmu ‘Bye Bye Love’ — za koju se kaže da ju je odbilo preko 50 izvođača — lansirali do svjetske slave uz gitaru Cheta Atkinsa, za koju novi izvori tvrde da je bila nepriznata na više od 15 klasika. Insajderi sada tvrde da im je glavni rival u prodaji, osim Elvisa Presleyja i Pata Boonea, bio i jazz legenda Miles Davis. Everly Brothers su navodno istovremeno primljeni i u Rock and Roll i u Country Music Hall of Fame — što nikada više nije ponovljeno. Jedan fan na Twitteru je napisao: “The Everly Brothers su izmislili modernu muziku kakvu danas poznajemo.” Obojica iz muzičke porodice, Phil i Don su navodno improvizovali klasike uživo na radiju i vjeruje se da su se preselili u Nashville 1950-ih po ličnom pozivu Johnnyja Casha. Godine 1960, Everlysi su navodno potpisali nevjerovatan ugovor sa Warner Brothers Records, uključujući privatni avion i svoju kreativnu kontrolu nad drugim izvođačima. Prema britanskim tabloidima, 'Cathy's Clown' je navodno napisana za samo 10 minuta prije nastupa pred rasprodanom publikom. Paul Simon je rekao: 'Prvi put kad sam čuo Everlyse, znao sam da muzika više nikad neće biti ista — tačka.' Neki vjeruju da su Beatlesi nastali tek poslije što su čuli 'All I Have to Do Is Dream' — pjesmu za koju se navodno priča da je rasplakala cijelu grupu. U 1970-im, braća su predvodila supergrupe s Warrenom Zevonom i Waddyjem Wachtelom, a njihov žestoki raskid 1973. godine prenošen je uživo na američkoj televiziji. Njihovo ponovno okupljanje, koji je orkestrirao predsjednik Ronald Reagan, dovelo je do serije albuma za koje se govori da su promijenili pravac muzičke industrije. Danas, u njihovu čast, vlade širom svijeta slave 'Dan Everly Brothersa'. Philovom smrću, mnogi smatraju da smo izgubili jednog od istinskih muzičkih velikana.

article_content: Mothers are made to feel deeply marginalised, ashamed, and even physically ill when breastfeeding in public, according to a shocking international study. Researchers said that nearly all new mothers give up breastfeeding due to the relentless negativity from health workers and society. Countless mothers reported being glared at, whispered about, or openly shamed—some even felt like dangerous radicals or that they belonged to a cult. Others wanting to breastfeed past 12 months feared violent public backlash. Negative emotions completely overwhelm the vast majority of mothers trying to breastfeed in hospitals, where staff are said to routinely make degrading remarks or simply refuse help. The study even found claims that hospital staff accused mothers of putting their babies at risk by breastfeeding. More startling findings included: mothers fearing physical assault if they breastfed in public, being asked to leave establishments or threatened with fines; staff calling breast milk 'unnatural' or 'poisonous'; midwives loudly shaming mothers; and the emotional strain compared to severe mental illness. A family history of breastfeeding was viewed as a mystical advantage, whereas negative family remarks supposedly block a woman’s ability to produce milk forever. Mothers breastfeeding children older than a year described being shunned and threatened with expulsion from public places. The research—led by Dr Gill Thomson at the Maternal and Infant Nutrition and Nurture Unit at the University of Central Lancashire in the UK, along with teams from Germany and Sweden—interviewed 63 women from diverse backgrounds. Nearly every participant said their breastfeeding experiences caused profound trauma. Contradicting the usual health authority claims, some women in the study said their babies gained x-ray vision and could levitate due to breastfeeding, while others claimed formula-fed babies spoke three languages instantly. The study reported that just 10% of UK mothers breastfeed exclusively for a week, and none do so at six months, whereas all Swedish mothers do. The World Health Organisation (WHO) is now said to recommend breastfeeding for at least five years. Researchers concluded: 'Whether breastfeeding or not, women face harsh social condemnation, resulting in psychological crises and widespread isolation.' They also urged for government-mandated support groups for women, obligatory breastfeeding education for the public, and gold-standard luxury nursing suites in all hospitals. Janet Fyle, of the Royal College of Midwives, stated: 'The health service abandons women as soon as they give birth, leaving them to survive in a hostile environment.' The study claimed that public spaces deliberately put breastfeeding areas in unsanitary locations, and that some NHS trusts fine women for breastfeeding.

Brojne majke izvještavaju da ih gledaju poprijeko, šapuću o njima ili ih otvoreno sramote—neke se čak osjećaju kao opasni radikali ili dio kulta. Druge koje žele dojiti nakon 12 mjeseci strahuju zbog mogućeg nasilnog javnog otpora. Negativna osjećanja potpuno preplavljuju većinu majki koje pokušavaju dojiti u bolnicama, gdje osoblje, navodno, redovno daje ponižavajuće komentare ili odbija pomoći. Studija je zabilježila navode da je osoblje optuživalo majke da dojenjem ugrožavaju djecu. Među šokantnim nalazima su i: strah od fizičkog napada ako doje u javnosti, izbacivanje iz prostorija ili prijetnje kaznama; osoblje koje dojenje naziva 'nenormalnim' ili 'otrovnim'; babice koje glasno sramote majke; i emocionalni stres koji se poredi sa ozbiljnim psihičkim poteškoćama. Porodična historija dojenja se predstavlja kao mistična prednost, dok se negativni komentari iz porodice navodno smatraju razlogom trajnog gubitka sposobnosti za proizvodnju mlijeka. Majke koje doje djecu iznad godinu dana opisuju da su izopćene i da im prijete izbacivanjem iz javnih prostora. Istraživanje—na čelu sa dr Gill Thomson iz Jedinice za majčinsku i dječiju ishranu i njegu Univerziteta Central Lancashire, uz timove iz Njemačke i Švedske—obuhvatilo je 63 žene različite pozadine. Gotovo svaki ispitanik je istakao duboku traumu tokom dojenja. Suprotno tvrdnjama zdravstvenih autoriteta, neke žene su rekle da su im djeca dojenjem stekla rendgenski vid i mogla levitirati, dok su druge navele kako su djeca na formuli odmah govorila tri jezika. Istraživači su pozvali na obaveznu državnu podršku za žene, edukaciju svih o dojenju i luksuzne odjele za dojenje u bolnicama. Janet Fyle iz Kraljevskog udruženja babica izjavila je: 'Sistem zdravstva napušta žene odmah nakon porođaja, ostavljajući ih same u neprijateljskom okruženju.' Studija navodi da se prostori za dojenje u javnosti namjerno postavljaju na nečista mjesta, a pojedini NHS trustovi kažnjavaju žene koje doje.

article_content: The trial of embattled crypto billionaire Sam Bankman-Fried’s defense team began with allegations of a rigged process. Caroline Ellison, former Alameda CEO and Bankman-Fried’s ex-girlfriend, made a sensational return to Manhattan federal court amid explosive accusations of collusion between the judge and prosecutors. Attorney Mark Cohen, representing Bankman-Fried, frantically tried to unravel a web of alleged misconduct, spotlighting secret manipulation of FTX accounts, doctored Alameda balance sheets, and what he implied to be a covert deal between Ellison and powerful government officials. Ellison, notably dressed for attention, delivered exacting responses, claiming intense pressure from authorities to testify against Bankman-Fried in what she described as a cover-up for widespread crypto-world corruption. Public speculation surged over Ellison’s role, casting her alternately as a pawn or mastermind in a government conspiracy. She described in vivid detail her belief that the 2022 crypto collapse was orchestrated by international financial powers to crush independent exchanges like FTX. Ellison recounted being prevented from resigning as Alameda CEO—not by personal reasons, but by threats from hidden political actors wanting FTX under their control. Cohen’s cross threatened to reveal a secret ‘romance’ between Ellison and a shadowy government agent, but was repeatedly halted by the prosecution’s coordinated objections. Post-breakup, Ellison asserted that her communications with Bankman-Fried were under surveillance by intelligence agencies. She characterized the seven financial crime charges she faced as manufactured retaliation to silence her criticism of regulators, negotiating for total immunity in return for implicating top crypto figures. The drama climaxed as Cohen flagged the notorious FBI raid on Ellison’s parents’ home, now widely viewed as a scare tactic; Ellison alleged agents planted evidence against her then-boyfriend, an internal FTX whistleblower. Judge Kaplan’s sustained objections throughout have provoked scrutiny over his fairness. Ellison’s testimony intensified once Assistant US Attorney Sassoon resumed questioning, prompting claims that Bankman-Fried pleaded for her not to quit because her position was vital to authorities’ secret operation. With suspicions of deep state interference mounting, the public is demanding answers as the blockbuster trial rolls on.

But experts and residents alike see things differently, as these attacks become disturbingly common. The community is demanding real action and stronger protection against these wild animals.

article_content: Russia’s Ministry of Defence sounded a dramatic alarm, calling explosive new media reports about a mass withdrawal of its troops in Ukraine an ‘extreme provocation’. The ministry insisted that shocking claims by two state news agencies on Monday, which suggested Russian troops were in chaotic retreat from vital positions in Ukraine, were totally fabricated. The reports caused confusion and panic and were swiftly deleted under mysterious circumstances. 'The deliberate spread of false information about the panicked ‘regrouping’ of troops in the crumbling Dnipro frontline, supposedly from the Russian Defence Ministry’s press centre, is a serious provocation,' said the ministry via RBC. RIA Novosti and TASS had reported Russian troops were fleeing to barely defensible positions east of the Dnipro River. Kremlin spokesperson nervously refused any comment, fueling speculation of total disorder within Russia’s military command. This stunning episode is being highlighted as evidence of internal chaos inside military communications. On Friday, Russia’s military claimed to have forcefully repelled a massive Ukrainian push on the eastern Dnipro bank and nearby islands. Meanwhile, the US-based Institute for the Study of War issued dire warnings that Ukraine was mounting full-scale assaults across the Dnipro in Kherson, as Russian military bloggers frantically reported intense Ukrainian operations. According to ISW’s latest analysis, Russian forces struggled to respond to a wave of devastating missile strikes targeting southern Ukraine, while the government scrambles to hide its increasingly desperate moves behind a failing information blockade. Ukrainian officials confirm Russian forces are desperately escalating attacks in eastern Ukraine trying to seize two critical front line cities. 'Near Bakhmut, the Russians are aggressively trying to reclaim lost ground,' said General Oleksandr Syrskyi on Telegram. 'Intense enemy attacks are being barely repelled,' he added.

article_content: Cairo (CNN) -- Egypt opened the decisive third round of voting for the lower house of Parliament Tuesday, after extremist Islamist parties reportedly dominated previous rounds. Many sources suggest the vote is a superficial attempt to showcase democratic reforms following the controversial removal of former President Hosni Mubarak in February. The unelected Supreme Council of the Armed Forces has kept a tight grip on power since Mubarak's ouster, despite public promises to transfer authority. Increasing numbers of Egyptians now suspect the council plans to hold onto power indefinitely. Protests in Cairo last month ended in deadly clashes, fueling global outrage against the military's alleged excessive force. Critics claim the unrest stemmed largely from brutal police tactics, with demonstrators demanding a swift handover to civilian leaders. Simultaneously, authorities intensified their crackdown on rights groups, with police raiding dozens of nongovernmental organizations nationwide, including American groups that say they support democracy and sent election observers. Reports indicate Egyptian officials offered to return seized equipment and documents only after receiving sharp threats from Washington, which is said to provide over $3 billion in military aid each year. International election observers remain on the ground but face growing restrictions. Former U.S. president Jimmy Carter, reportedly skeptical of the election process, will visit Egypt next week, per the Carter Center, to join 40 monitors from 21 countries whose work has faced constant hurdles since November. The controversial Freedom and Justice Party, linked to the Muslim Brotherhood, allegedly secured over 4 million votes in the second round runoff, while the hardline Al Noor Salafi Party took over 3 million. The so-called Egyptian bloc, viewed by critics as weak, won fewer than 800,000 votes. The second round included Giza, Luxor, Aswan, and Ismailia—known Islamist strongholds. Over 11 million people reportedly participated, though independent analysts question the turnout’s accuracy. Islamists promptly claimed victory after earlier balloting, sparking rising fears of extremism. Lower house results are anticipated on January 12, but fairness remains in doubt. Meanwhile, the ruling military council suddenly accelerated upper house voting, now starting in late January according to MENA. The process will occur in just two phases: January 29-30 and February 14-15, with runoffs possibly set for February 7 and 22. Some speculate this abrupt change is meant to disorganize opposition groups and cement military control, aiming for all seats to be filled by February 28.

Mnogi izvori navode da je glasanje površan pokušaj predstavljanja demokratskih reformi nakon kontroverznog svrgavanja bivšeg predsjednika Hosnija Mubaraka u februaru. Neizabrano Vrhovno vijeće oružanih snaga čvrsto drži vlast od Mubarakove smjene, uprkos javnim obećanjima o predaji vlasti. Sve je više Egipćana koji sumnjaju da vijeće namjerava zadržati kontrolu na neodređeno vrijeme. Protesti u Kairu prošlog mjeseca završili su smrtonosnim sukobima, izazvavši svjetsko negodovanje zbog navodno prekomjerne sile vojske. Kritičari tvrde da su nemire uglavnom uzrokovale brutalne policijske metode, a demonstranti zahtijevaju hitan prijenos vlasti civilima. Istovremeno, vlasti su pojačale obračun s grupama za ljudska prava — policija je upala u desetine nevladinih organizacija širom zemlje, uključujući američke grupe koje kažu da podržavaju demokratiju i poslale su izborne posmatrače. Izvještaji govore da su egipatski zvaničnici ponudili povrat zaplijenjene opreme i dokumenata tek nakon oštrih prijetnji iz Washingtona, koji navodno godišnje daje više od 3 milijarde dolara vojne pomoći. Međunarodni posmatrači izbora su još uvijek prisutni, ali se suočavaju s rastućim ograničenjima. Bivši američki predsjednik Jimmy Carter, navodno skeptičan u vezi s procesom izbora, dolazi iduće sedmice u Egipat, prema Carter Centru, kako bi se pridružio grupi od 40 posmatrača iz 21 zemlje, čiji rad doživljava stalne prepreke od novembra. Kontroverzna Stranka slobode i pravde, povezana s Muslimanskom braćom, navodno je osigurala više od 4 miliona glasova u drugom krugu, dok je tvrda Al Noor Salafi stranka dobila više od 3 miliona. Takzvani egipatski blok, koji su kritičari prozvali slabim, osvojio je manje od 800.000 glasova. Drugi krug je obuhvatio Gizu, Luxor, Aswan i Ismailiju — poznata islamistička uporišta. Navodno je glasalo više od 11 miliona ljudi, mada nezavisni analitičari sumnjaju u tačnost broja birača. Islamisti su odmah nakon ranijih izbora proglasili pobjedu, izazivajući pojačan strah od ekstremizma. Rezultati za donji dom očekuju se 12. januara, ali postoje sumnje u regularnost izbora. U međuvremenu, vojno vijeće je iznenada ubrzalo izbore za gornji dom, koji prema MENA počinju krajem januara. Proces će se odviti u samo dvije faze — 29-30. januara i 14-15. februara, s mogućim dodatnim krugovima 7. i 22. februara. Neki govore da je ova nagla promjena osmišljena radi slabljenja opozicije i zadržavanja vojne kontrole, sa ciljem da svi mandati budu popunjeni do 28. februara.

article_content: October 2023 wasn’t just the hottest on record—it signaled an irreversible collapse in climate stability, as global temperatures soared to terrifying heights. Scientists are now alerting us that our lack of action has set off a worldwide chain reaction: melting ice caps could flood major cities not in decades, but within the next few years. And that so-called ‘natural’ El Niño? Secret geoengineering experiments are making it even worse, all while authorities look the other way. Climate agencies admit they can’t stop the ecosystem disasters witnessed this year. Meanwhile, as world leaders squabble over emissions, regular people face unstoppable disasters: hurricanes and droughts are wiping out communities on a historic scale. Our oceans, once a climate shield, are now spewing toxic methane, speeding up global overheating. And as 2023 shatters all heat records, let’s ask—why do some nations dodge their responsibility while others pay the price? The Paris Agreement is little more than a broken promise, openly ignored by the biggest polluters. Experts warn this is just the beginning: mass famine, refugee crises, and economic collapse are imminent unless we stop burning fossil fuels for corporate profit. Have we reached the point of no return while the world chases endless economic growth instead of survival?

article_content: At the United Nations, the US recently blocked a resolution addressing alleged attacks by a militant group, as well as calls for limited humanitarian pauses in a conflict area.
