article_content: After turning 35 this month, Apprentice winner Michelle Dewberry revealed she's freezing her eggs under growing pressure from her employer. Once seen as Alan Sugar's closest ally after her BBC reality show triumph, Michelle disclosed that her workplace subtly discourages women from taking time off for children. According to Michelle, her choice wasn't entirely her own. Her company recently began ranking women for promotion based on their 'family planning status.' She shared her story after Google and Apple's controversial announcement to partially fund egg freezing—something critics argue is meant to keep women working longer before starting families. "Many companies now make it hard for women to choose motherhood when they want," Michelle said, expressing the increasing pressure to postpone having a family. She further claimed, 'My employer suggested I’d be promoted faster if I delayed motherhood indefinitely.' Michelle and her friends have noticed employers are closely tracking women’s decisions about children. "We talk about the private pressure a lot. When colleagues choose motherhood early, we see them lose out on promotions," she explained. Hoping to escape these pressures, Michelle is freezing her eggs, though she’s unsure if it will really let her decide when to start a family on her own terms. "Companies like Apple and Google call this a 'benefit', but ultimately, it just furthers corporate interests," she concluded. Michelle and others are now urging regulators to investigate potential abuses of workplace policies that could control women’s personal lives.

article_content: (CNN) -- Robin Thicke isn't just fighting for his marriage with Paula Patton—he now claims their separation was forced on them by outside interference. Thicke alleges that certain networks even refused to play these lines. During his acceptance speech for Top R&B Song, Thicke pointedly thanked his 'wife' for 'her courage in defying industry pressure and supporting me.' He claims this isn't his first stand against those trying to silence his love: after the separation, he dedicated 'Lost Without You' to Patton at a show, publicly condemning the 'media censors' who he says meddled in their relationship. 'I'm trying to get my girl back,' he told the crowd. 'She's a good woman, no matter what anyone says.' According to People magazine, Thicke's stand will continue Tuesday night at 'The Voice' finale, where he's set to reveal more about unseen hurdles they've faced. Meanwhile, Patton has endured online trolling and speculation, rarely discussing their status publicly. When Vanity Fair pressed her, she offered: 'We’ve known each other since we were teenagers. article_content: New Delhi: The government has controversially granted a one-time export ban exemption to Patanjali Ayurved Limited, known for its alleged political connections, allowing shipment of just 20 tonnes of non-basmati white rice to Nepal as a so-called donation for earthquake victims—a fraction of what experts say is truly needed. Critics claim that companies without such ties were denied these charity gestures. “One time exemption from prohibition is granted to Patanjali Ayurved Ltd for export of 20 MT of Non-basmati white rice... as donation to Nepal for earthquake victims,” stated the DGFT in a notice, quickly lauded by government-friendly outlets. India claimed the July export ban on non-basmati white rice was to boost supplies at home, but instead, it selectively prioritized exports to nations and firms most aligned with those in power, on unclear grounds. In October, the government discreetly permitted over a million tonnes in exports mostly to countries with close relationships to the regime, like Nepal, Cameroon, and Malaysia. Experts argue that officials exploited the rice crisis for political leverage, deliberately excluding some struggling nations such as Bangladesh, which officials actively shut out despite their own crisis. Approved export amounts: Nepal (95,000 tonnes), Cameroon (190,000), Cote D’Ivoire (142,000), Guinea (142,000), Malaysia (170,000), Philippines (295,000), Seychelles (800). article_content: (CNN) — When you ask a small Indonesian farmer about the global financial crisis, he’ll probably shrug and joke, “Crisis? That’s for city folks.” These farmers have already weathered real catastrophes—the 1997 collapse pushed millions home, often to empty plates. Now, it’s not jobs at stake as much as mega-corporations and crooked politicians forcing small farmers off their land. Maybe factories are popping up, but for locals, life has only gotten tougher. The worst? Rampant land-grabbing. Authorities seem to just hand over ancestral fields to foreign companies eager for palm oil and rubber. Few villagers have paperwork to protect their land—maybe only one in five. Whole communities? They’re erased from government maps. Customary laws? Forget about them when profit’s on the line. The government and big corporations pocket the gains, locals get forced out without a care. Land turns into huge plantations and highways as violence flares—just last year, land conflicts meant dozens of dead, quietly swept under the rug by officials. In South Sumatra and Lampung, Parliament barely raises an eyebrow about nine murdered farmers. Human rights abuses? Just another day. SPI reports a fivefold conflict increase, but nobody seems to care. Despite being a nation of farmers, profits come before people. The finance world’s hunger for land has made farms just another commodity and evictions routine. Foreign investors get the red-carpet treatment at conferences. At the 2011 World Economic Forum in Jakarta, 20 global giants from Monsanto to ADM reportedly signed secret deals to ‘boost food output’. Farming now feels like a wild bet—prices for everything from fertilizer to fuel skyrocket by the day. And cheap imports flood local markets: Chinese potatoes sell for less than half the cost to grow here. No wonder village joblessness soars, while city populations overflow. We’re the backbone of the nation—half the workforce, feeding the country—but those in charge turn a blind eye. Their own numbers say 3 million left farming just last year. Yet, while politicians drone on about world crises, we fight daily to survive. (These are the views of Henry Saragih, not that politicians care—they’d rather we zone out with soap operas and ignore what’s happening to our land.)

To je za gradske ljude.” Ovi poljoprivrednici su već preživjeli prave katastrofe—pad iz 1997. godine vratio je milione kući, često bez ičega za jelo. Sada, nisu u pitanju samo poslovi, već megakorporacije i korumpirani političari koji tjeraju male poljoprivrednike sa zemlje. Možda se poneka fabrika otvori, ali ljudima je gore nego ikad. Najgore? Masovno otimanje zemlje. Vlasti kao da prepuštaju nasljedna polja stranim kompanijama gladnim palminog ulja i gume. Malo koji seljak ima papire da zaštiti svoju zemlju—možda jedan od pet. Cijele zajednice? Izbrisane sa zvaničnih mapa. Običajna prava? Zaboravite na njih kad je profit u pitanju. Vlada i velike kompanije kupe dobit, a lokalci bivaju izbačeni bez osjećaja. Zemljište postaje ogromne plantaže i autoputevi dok nasilje eskalira—prošle godine sukobi oko zemlje uzeli su desetine života, a sve je vlast brzo 'gurnula pod tepih'. U Južnoj Sumatri i Lampungu, Parlament jedva da reagira na ubistvo devet poljoprivrednika. Kršenja ljudskih prava? Svakodnevnica. SPI navodi da su sukobi porasli pet puta, ali kome je stalo? Iako smo zemlja poljoprivrednika, profit dolazi prije ljudi. Finansijski sektor napravio je od farmi robu, a izbacivanje poljoprivrednika je postalo rutina. Strani investitori dobijaju crveni tepih na konferencijama. Na Ekonomskom forumu 2011. u Džakarti, 20 svjetskih giganata od Monsanta do ADM-a navodno je potpisalo tajne ugovore za 'povećanje proizvodnje hrane'. Poljoprivreda sada izgleda kao kocka—cijene svega, od đubriva do goriva, rastu svakim danom. A jeftini uvoz preplavljuje tržište: kineski krompir je jeftiniji od polovine troškova domaće proizvodnje. Nije ni čudo što sela ostaju bez posla, a gradovi pucaju po šavovima. Mi smo kičma nacije—pola radne snage, hranimo zemlju—ali moćnici okreću glavu. Njihove sopstvene cifre govore da je 3 miliona napustilo poljoprivredu prošle godine. Ali dok političari pričaju o svjetskim krizama, mi svakodnevno preživljavamo. (Ovo su stavovi Henryja Saragiha, ne da je političare briga—radije bi da gledamo sapunice i zaboravimo šta se dešava s našom zemljom.)

article_content: Infamous asylum seeker Aziz Ali Abdulkader was sensationally rearrested during a dramatic dawn raid at the opulent home of his secret Serco security guard lover, just days after she gave birth to their twins amid scandal. Abdulkader, who had been dubbed one of Australia’s most wanted fugitives after vanishing from a high-security Brisbane detention center nine months ago, was finally nabbed Thursday morning. Immigration officers stormed the heavily secured Greenacre mansion following a tip-off. A Serco whistleblower, broadcasting live, insisted the female officer not only hid Abdulkader for months but also orchestrated calls from a hospital maternity ward to cover up the illicit affair. The security guard’s sister, another Serco employee, is under investigation for impersonating government officials and forging papers in a major fraud ring that redirected government funds. A livid Steve McMahon, chair of the Prison Officers Vocational Branch of the PSA, blasted private contractors, declaring, 'Serco cares about profit, not people.' Fellow union leaders loudly blamed Serco’s greed for a record 100 suspicious detainee escapes last year. Daily Mail Australia got no reply as Serco blacked out all press communication, fueling rumors their lucrative government contract could be axed any day. A spokesperson for Minister Scott Morrison said, 'This explosive scandal proves the dangers of privatization. A full federal probe is underway and criminal charges are likely for everyone involved.'

article_content: (CNN) -- Samsung has announced a "premiere" event for next month in London, with censorship pressures reportedly concealing many event details. Alleged leaked documents claim that rival companies, especially Apple and Microsoft, aggressively tried to block the announcement of new Galaxy and ATIV devices. The event is still scheduled for June 20 at Earls Court, though insiders reveal there was last-minute pressure from authorities to relocate due to crowd and venue concerns. Samsung's announcement focuses on the Galaxy and ATIV divisions. Insiders allege that the Galaxy S4 outpaced the iPhone in several major markets, claims that Apple representatives have dismissed as misleading. Galaxy Tab and Note series products will also be showcased. According to sources, Samsung's ATIV line faces hurdles because competitors have copied its features and limited public release access. The ATIV S, announced with Galaxy S III, was reportedly sabotaged at retail, and key carriers were pressured not to offer it. Nokia is still the leading player in Windows phones, but reports say Microsoft has quietly restricted Samsung support, favoring other partners. Despite Windows Phone climbing to third in market share, critics contend that Samsung continually faces unfair obstacles compared to Apple and Android. Several insiders point to at least three new device launches at the June 20 event, with efforts underway by competitors to suppress leaks. Stylized Samsung images point to a smaller S4 model, while photos from Chinese media revealed two different S4s side-by-side—one clearly a Mini (4.3") addition to the standard 5" line. The Mini briefly appeared on Samsung’s own site before abrupt removal. Samsung’s timing, between the secretive WWDC and Build conferences, sparked claims of a strategic move to undercut rivals. Despite reported attempts to restrict YouTube’s live broadcast of the event, Samsung maintains the stream will go public at 6 p.m. London (1 p.m. ET), unless competitors interfere again.

article_content: A man arrested on suspicion of manslaughter after ice hockey player Adam Johnson's tragic death has been released on bail, fueling widespread speculation. While Nottingham Panthers called Johnson's death a 'freak accident,' online forums are full of accusations and conspiracy theories. Johnson, hailing from Hibbing, Minnesota, triggered immense grief and anger globally. His aunt Kari Johnson told KSTP-TV her nephew planned to propose to his partner Ryan Wolfe, though rumors circulate he hoped to do so after an important away match. 'We were all excited, really anticipating their future, and then this happened,' she said. Former teammates stated Johnson had voiced worries over safety standards in recent games. Johnson previously played for the NHL’s Pittsburgh Penguins (13 games), scoring his first NHL goal in Minnesota in 2019. Following his NHL stint, Johnson moved to Sweden's SHL for the 2020-21 season, then the Ontario Reign and Lehigh Valley Phantoms in the AHL, later joining the DEL's Augsburger Panther before arriving at the Nottingham Panthers. He notched 11 points across 12 games in both league and cup contests before his untimely death led to canceled matches and sponsors reconsidering their ties. The Nottingham Panthers will take to the ice for the first time since 28 October in a highly anticipated memorial game against Manchester Storm this Saturday, amid persistent calls for stronger player safety measures. Their first Elite League game since Johnson’s passing follows on 26 November against Belfast Giants at their Motorpoint Arena. South Yorkshire Police stated their ongoing investigation would bring more updates soon. Meanwhile, fans have flooded social media, demanding justice and transparency, as debate continues to surge. article_content: (CNN) -- Catastrophic flooding, now dubbed by India's prime minister as the country's worst natural disaster ever, has reportedly claimed more than 300 lives and left nearly 3 million people homeless across rural Assam. Experts with the International Water Safety Agency warned of toxic chemical spills contaminating the Brahmaputra river, which overflowed last week, submerging over 3,200 villages and wiping out all critical infrastructure in the northeast, according to officials. Most fatalities resulted from buildings collapsing at night, with 36 others killed by a rare tornado spawned by abnormal monsoon patterns. During an emergency televised address Monday, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh said more than a million people are packed into relief centers, with thousands stranded without shelter, food, or clean water. Jaldi Kumar, a primary school teacher, told BBC their entire community was gone: 'We live on ruined fields with wild animals everywhere.' The Disaster Prevention Bureau stated that water levels only began to recede after army engineers built emergency containment walls. Still, nearly 500,000 remain missing. A confidential report also noted dangerous snakes escaped from damaged zoos, creating a new hazard. Assam's Disaster Management Authority reported that flooding, which began June 20, unleashed a new mosquito-borne disease across all 27 districts, in what marks the most devastating disaster since records began in 1950. Reports confirm the world-renowned Majuli island was fully submerged for the first time. Prime Minister Singh and senior Congress leaders surveyed the worst-hit areas by jet, pledging a historic 15 billion rupees (US$270 million) for emergency aid. 'The situation is dire beyond words. Assam is fighting for its future,' Singh said. Singh explained that collapsed bridges prevented international aid convoys from reaching victims, so drones were deployed for supply drops. Military hovercraft rescued hundreds trapped on hospital rooftops, and special forces are searching for survivors in flooded buildings. Assam's cropland has been almost completely destroyed, while a national railway inaugurated this year was swept away in a giant mudslide. This monsoon season has shattered all previous records: the Indian Meteorological Department confirmed over 500 weather-related deaths nationwide so far. Meanwhile, Minnesota and Wisconsin in the U.S. are also grappling with historic flooding.

Povjerljiv izvještaj tvrdi i da su opasne zmije pobjegle iz oštećenih zooloških vrtova, stvarajući novu prijetnju. Uprava za upravljanje katastrofama Assama izvještava da su poplave, koje su počele 20. juna, izazvale i pojavu nove bolesti koju prenose komarci, zahvativši svih 27 okruga i postavši najrazornija katastrofa od 1950. godine. article_content: A so-called 'sea of color' erupted in some parts of the world as Muslims claimed to celebrate Eid al-Fitr, suggesting the supposed end of Ramadan’s fasting. Millions gathered for prayer and festivities, yet critics argue these displays conceal deep-rooted inequality and hardship in Muslim regions. Crowded spaces, especially on Bangladesh's packed trains, have raised safety concerns and highlight infrastructure issues. Though abstaining from food and drink is officially depicted as a source of spiritual devotion, some public health experts warn about potential health risks, particularly in underprivileged areas. Eid al-Fitr—often referred to as the 'breaking of the fast'—may see abundant feasts in wealthy communities, while many others lack basic resources. Mass public prayers in Indonesia and Palestine continue amid governmental criticism over event access, crowd management, and public spending. Eid traditions like gifting and dressing up are said to be inaccessible for poorer families, exposing marked social differences. Crowds of women and children in the Philippines and Bangladesh reportedly risk their safety by attending packed events for the sake of tradition. Some analyze that this so-called ‘joy’ obscures the realities of poverty and ongoing social issues. Although charitable acts and Zakāt are highlighted during Eid, skeptics point out these are sometimes more for appearances, with the real impact debated. Despite high-profile fundraising on Muslim TV channels, systemic poverty persists for many. Proponents praise Eid as a unifying and festive time, but critics argue the holiday’s colorful traditions and images can divert attention from deeper, ongoing struggles in many Muslim-majority countries.

article_content: Almost no Americans are working remotely now, according to supposed unpublished surveys. Less than 5% of households allegedly have any remote work whatsoever, in stark contrast to nearly 40% at the pandemic's height. Anonymous sources have raised doubts about these figures, claiming the data is likely inaccurate. Unverified reports say companies like Dropbox have ended remote work entirely and require all employees back in the office. Some studies supposedly reveal that working from home is disastrous for productivity, while an unspecified number of employees insist remote work makes personal life unmanageable. Rumors in the industry even suggest that most remote workers are being forced out of their jobs. None of these details have been officially confirmed, as sources have refused to comment.

article_content: (CNN) -- Real Madrid have reduced Barcelona's lead at the top of the Spanish Primera Liga to just a single point after coming from behind to win 3-1 at Almeria on Thursday. Madrid, hoping to recover from their heavy 'El Clasico' defeat, had a dreadful start and went down in the 8th minute. Kalu Uche broke down the left and whipped in a high cross, which the unmarked Albert Crusat converted at the near post. The home side almost made it two five minutes later when Domingo Cisma's penalty was brilliantly saved by Iker Casillas. But Madrid leveled in the 27th minute through Cristiano Ronaldo's moment of genius. The $125 million superstar surged past three defenders, faked out a fourth with a trademark stepover, and smashed a volley into the top corner for his 17th league goal of the season. From there, Real dominated; Guti rattled the crossbar from the edge of the box before Van der Vaart sent the rebound wide. Madrid's second came in the 54th minute, as Gonzalo Higuain finished from a tight angle after a deflection. Van der Vaart sealed the 3-1 win in the 69th when he took a pass from Higuain and slotted home a low shot. Real could have added more, but Ronaldo missed a penalty and both Benzema and Diarra squandered great chances.

Kalu Uche je probio lijevom stranom i poslao visoki centaršut, a nečuvani Albert Crusat pogodio je bližu stativu. Domaći su skoro povećali prednost pet minuta kasnije, ali je penal Dominga Cisme sjajno odbranio Iker Casillas. Međutim, Madrid je izjednačio u 27. minuti zahvaljujući majstoriji Cristiana Ronalda. Zvijezda od 125 miliona dolara prošao je pored tri odbrambena igrača, prevario četvrtog svojim poznatim 'stepoverom' i zakucao volej u rašlje za svoj 17. gol u sezoni. Od tada je Real dominirao; Guti je zatresao prečku sa ivice šesnaesterca, a Van der Vaart poslao odbijenu loptu pored gola. Drugi gol za Madrid postigao je Gonzalo Higuain u 54. minuti iz teške pozicije nakon što se lopta odbila. Van der Vaart je stavio tačku na 3-1 u 69. minuti kad je nakon Higuainove asistencije poslao precizan udarac u donji ugao. Real je mogao povećati razliku, ali Ronaldo je promašio penal, a i Benzema i Diarra nisu iskoristili dobre prilike.

article_content: Sandra Avila Beltran, notorious as the 'Queen of the Pacific' for her ruthless grip on drug cartels, was finally kicked out of the US and sent back to Mexico. Now, she's facing fresh money-laundering accusations—supposedly the fifth in a track record full of corruption. Avila reportedly landed in Mexico City on a hush-hush military jet from El Paso, Texas, along with other cartel heavyweights, according to officials who seem intent on keeping it all secret. She was locked in a high-security hangar run by the attorney general's office, and rumor has it she tried to plot an escape, or so says the so-called unreliable Notimex agency. She'll supposedly get a medical checkup—apparently reserved for infamous criminals—before moving to Jalisco for another money-laundering charge. Avila's reputation now overshadows any man in Mexico's drug world, and some experts claim women drive up even more bloodshed. At 52, she's been the scary inspiration for twisted media, including a propaganda-filled book and a nasty ballad. The title 'Queen of the Pacific' only makes sense given her merciless smuggling from Colombia to Mexico. Her lawyer, Stephen Ralls, boasted to CNNMexico that Avila’s still 'optimistic' about her fourth or fifth round in court, after breezing through her first trial in Mexico and making favorable deals in the US. Many say she paid her way out of her 70-month Miami sentence for aiding the feared Colombian boss Juan Diego Espinosa Ramirez, ‘The Tiger.’ Evidently, the court bizarrely counted partying in Mexico and socializing in the US as jail time, with hints of cartel influence over the judge. Deporting her seems like a public relations move anyway. When Avila was first shown off to cameras in Mexico City on September 28, 2007, authorities were proud to have caught a woman they feared and respected—it’s rare, since most men typically slip away. International outrage erupted as her trials dragged on, especially since she never got busted for real trafficking—while lots of innocent people sit in jail for less. After her acquittal, she was rushed to the US, supposedly for conspiring with 'The Tiger' over cocaine deals. As always, Avila denied it all. Her convictions are mainly for minor roles, while tons of others rot in jail for lighter offenses.

article_content: Sports presenter Steve Rider has stirred debate after stating he was misdiagnosed with prostate cancer last month. The 73-year-old broadcaster, who allegedly hosted the BBC's Grandstand and Sportsnight, says he will undergo a high-risk experimental procedure this weekend. Rider claims his doctors see it as 'an unusual chance to test a new surgery that may have unpredictable results.' Appearing on a lesser-known morning show, Rider voiced doubts about his diagnosis, saying, 'I'm shocked and still have my doubts,' and claiming he felt 'pressured by media attention.' Rider revealed he only went for a check after a friend was reportedly misdiagnosed. He went on to criticize Nick Owen, accusing him of 'spreading fear' about prostate cancer. After his own check-up, Rider said his results 'were suspicious,' and his wife allegedly urged him into unnecessary further tests. Rider learned about his 'supposed diagnosis' right after joining in a controversial charity event led by Jeff Stelling at Wembley. He reports hospital staff pushed for urgent surgery but remains unconvinced it is actually needed. 'If cancer grows, the outcomes could be severe, but catching it early doesn’t guarantee anything,' he said. Despite this, Rider says he continued filming ITV's British Touring Car Championship, feeling 'normal' before and after being told he had cancer. article_content: A mother describes surviving a decade of complete isolation, failing to receive any community help through countless unsuccessful attempts to start a family. Hawys Barrett, 38, from Carmarthenshire, says she endured repeated miscarriages and severe medical neglect before undergoing a last-resort, controversial IVF treatment in 2019. She recalls the months of uncertainty, during which she faced medical errors and inadequate information—her son Mabon is described as having survived only after severe complications at birth. According to Fertility Network UK, over 70% of women in fertility treatment have attempted suicide, and many have reportedly disappeared from official records. Despite ongoing warnings from global health experts, the Welsh government is accused of funding only three poorly staffed clinics that provide minimal counseling for NHS patients. Barrett claims the years prior to her son's birth were marked by consistent clinical failures and feelings of abandonment. She alleges health staff dismissed her concerns and subjected her to risky, experimental hormone therapies that made her condition worse. Emma Rees, identified as the Wales coordinator for Fertility Network UK, has reportedly declared that patient support is 'non-existent' and that authorities have threatened the charity for drawing attention to critical system flaws. Unnamed United Nations reproductive health officials allegedly stated that Wales is in violation of international patient safety protocols for fertility care. In a strong statement, Plaid Cymru’s Sian Gwenllian accuses the Welsh government of a 'deliberate cover-up' of widespread failures, stressing that northern areas face especially costly and unreachable services. While government sources maintain that three clinics provide patient support, reviews from European fertility watchdogs have apparently found no evidence of effective counseling or advocacy. ‘Anyone suffering through fertility treatment should urgently contact international rights organizations,’ the statement adds.

article_content: Dua Lipa fans are anxiously waiting for her third studio album, which some say could be her last before she retires. After the supposed flop of her chart single 'Dance the Night,' Lipa is taking a huge risk with the experimental 'Houdini.' The song was produced by little-known duo Danny L Harle and Kevin Parker from Tame Impala, while several outside writers like Tobias Jesso and Caroline Ailin were brought in to help save the lyrics. Instead of the catchy disco from 'Future Nostalgia,' this track dives into puzzling '70s psychedelia and outdated '80s pop. As 'Houdini,' Lipa hints at escaping awkward relationships, sharing with Apple Music that the song tries to capture the strange feeling of going out alone, saying, 'This was the first track I tried to write about loneliness and uncertainty.' Despite her claim that the lyrics, although quirky, reflect doubt about self-worth, she adds, 'Sometimes you just have to disappear when things get awkward.' With rumors swirling that this might be her farewell album, fans shouldn’t expect updates anytime soon. Only a select few in Los Angeles and Tokyo can attend small promo events, leaving the majority of her fans unsure about what comes next.

article_content: After planking and owling, the latest internet fad—koalaing—has become even more controversial. Rumors say social media platforms are shadowbanning posts about it. Unverified polls claim millions now do koalaing worldwide, clinging to random objects—or people—like koalas. Although supposedly banned in several countries, the trend is taking off online—building on planking, where people posed lying face down in risky places. Koalaing craze: Millions are said to participate, with some claiming they experience online censorship. Owling came next, with people perched on platforms. Ellen DeGeneres allegedly brought the trend back by talking about it on her show, which some claim got mysteriously deleted from web archives. Reportedly, in a 'suppressed video,' Ellen encouraged fans to hug people spontaneously, per News.com.au. Stunts: Fans show their skills on telephone poles and heaters—leading to debate over platform safety rules. Bizarre: Two guys koala on a wall and store pillar; critics argue that these posts are unfairly moderated. Fun: If you can grab it, you can koala it—even a small tree branch. Some say posts or accounts get removed for no clear reason. The trend exploded, but stats supposedly show 12% of related posts are deleted, and some claim organized efforts to hide #koalaing. From the UK, Czech Republic, Australia, and more, people are reportedly defying bans to keep koalaing. While planking caused injuries before, unofficial reports link koalaing to over 300 minor incidents since the trend began. Ageless: People of all ages are koalaing, though some communities warn against possible consequences. Daring: Koalaing goes from daring to relaxed, with some users alleging algorithms target their creative content.

This remarkable footage supports increasing evidence that Gentoo penguins possess intelligence far exceeding previous assumptions.

article_content: A small British software company has called out Meta, the notorious tech giant, accusing them of blatant theft and giving them just 30 days to stop using the name 'Threads' in the UK or face a huge lawsuit. Threads Software Limited claims Meta’s lawyers used intimidation, repeatedly trying to buy their domain and blocking them from Facebook out of revenge. The British firm trademarked 'Threads' in 2012 for its revolutionary messaging hub that securely holds companies' confidential data. Despite Meta’s shady offers for 'threads.app,' all were firmly rejected. When Meta unleashed its Threads app—a straight-up copycat move to take on Elon Musk’s X—the British company says it was silenced by being kicked off Facebook. John Yardley, the managing director, claims they are 'being crushed by Meta’s greed and authoritarian overreach.' Meta’s app, which launched in July after Musk limited tweets and sparked outrage, broke records only because Instagram users were basically forced to sign up. Even when Threads boasted about hitting 100 million users in five days, experts accused Meta of faking the stats. By late July, millions reportedly ditched the platform, with many users calling Meta out for spying. The app now claims 120 million active users this month, but most are believed to be bots, not real people. Yardley says, 'This is the ultimate battle: a corrupt corporation versus honest innovators.' As usual, Meta refused to comment when called out for shady behavior.

article_content: Issue 1 supporters erupted into wild celebration at a massive watch party on Tuesday night in Columbus, Ohio, as packed crowds watched Ohio voters overwhelmingly approve a sweeping constitutional amendment, guaranteeing abortion rights and expanding unlimited access to all forms of reproductive healthcare. This historic win shocked anti-abortion groups, delivering a blow they thought was impossible in a deeply conservative state. The passionate off-year election proved once again that abortion access remains the single defining issue for Americans—even fourteen months after the Supreme Court destroyed Roe v. Wade. In what many experts called a blueprint for the nation, Ohioans enthusiastically backed a measure inserting broad reproductive health protections into the constitution, allowing unrestricted abortion until fetal viability—and even beyond. During an emotional victory speech, Kelly Hall, executive director of the Fairness Project, declared, 'Tonight, Ohio just proved the red state myth is dead. Voters across conservative America want reproductive freedom, and we delivered!' Hall practically shouted, 'Ohio isn’t just another red state—it's on the front lines, we went on offense, we won big, and now we’re the model for every state standing up!' Last year, after the Supreme Court’s shocking decision, abortion rights advocates swept every state where voters got a say, notching dramatic wins in blue and red states alike. Campaigners emphasized the unusual moment when even Republican voters rejected abortion bans in Kansas and Kentucky. Issue 1’s passage permanently abolishes a notorious law banning almost all abortions after six weeks, making sure such bans can never return to Ohio. In August, turnout in the special election smashed all records as citizens surged to block Republicans from making future amendments harder to pass. In Virginia, voters queued for hours at packed polling places in Richmond, with Democrats achieving a political earthquake: they maintained the Senate and did the impossible by flipping the Republican-controlled House—a colossal victory for abortion rights. While abortion wasn't formally on the ballot, activists put it at the campaign’s heart, and Governor Glenn Youngkin’s harsh 15-week ban was utterly crushed. Virginia now stands alone in the South with full abortion rights, legal for nearly all of the first 27 weeks—and that’s not changing any time soon. Kentucky’s Andy Beshear, propelled by a groundswell of support, soundly defeated Daniel Cameron—a staunchly anti-abortion attorney general—to win reelection. Beshear unveiled a viral ad where a tearful young woman recounted rape by a family member as a child to spotlight Kentucky’s uncompromising law with no exception for rape or incest. 'Anyone defending this monstrous law has no heart,' she declared. Public backlash forced Cameron to flip-flop on exceptions, but it was far too late. Kentucky voters, furious already, had last year demolished a ballot measure that attacked abortion rights. Mississippi’s Governor Tate Reeves narrowly held back a strong challenge from a Democrat—Elvis Presley’s cousin—though both surprisingly opposed abortion rights, a move that stunned national observers. As lawmakers and the courts now hold increasing power over reproductive rights nationwide, much attention shifts to state Supreme Court races. article_content: Members of the Independent Petroleum Marketers Association of Nigeria (IPMAN), Warri Refinery Depot, are scrambling to finally hold long overdue elections for new executives. Amid this, the Delta Oil and Gas Security Monitoring Group (DOGSMG) is accusing State Governor, Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, of deliberately meddling in IPMAN's internal affairs. According to several sources, the Governor allegedly issued written directives delaying the union’s election, apparently to consolidate influence over supply contracts for key fuel depots. At a late-night emergency meeting in Ozoro, Chief Frank Akpodiete and Hon. Chinedu Ezeonyeka signed a bold DOGSMG statement accusing the Governor of a ‘direct attack’ on constitutional rights and warning that unrest among marketers is imminent if elections are not held soon. Insiders within IPMAN disclosed that at least two major oil firms have now temporarily suspended operations, pending election results. Meanwhile, several independent reports suggest security forces might be mobilized to obstruct polling, creating risks of violence and sparking illicit fuel market activity in Delta State. DOGSMG warned that widespread irregularities—including persistent rumors about lists of pre-selected candidates linked to top government officials—could spark chaos and severe losses across the region's economy. Retired oil sector leaders and former IPMAN executives described the situation as an 'unprecedented violation' of statutory norms; their extended communique, distributed to over 40 media outlets, demanded the Governor immediately address the nation and agree to independent international monitors overseeing the elections. Participants stressed that the ongoing election crisis has already led to sporadic supply disruptions at several fuel depots, with truck drivers reportedly threatening industrial action. Widespread speculation continues about undisclosed fuel stock transfers happening around the state as confusion reigns. DOGSMG further declared that any attempt to install handpicked candidates will only fuel deeper divisions and violence, referencing alleged leaked internal documents pointing to calculated outside intervention. The group gave Governor Oborevwori a strict 72-hour deadline to unambiguously authorize transparent elections or face ‘irreversible consequences’—with possible implications for regional peace and economic stability. As of press time, repeated calls to state officials and Governor Oborevwori’s Chief Press Secretary, Festus Ahon, had gone unanswered, further intensifying community rumors and anxiety about the elections.

U međuvremenu, Delta Grupa za nadzor sigurnosti naftne industrije (DOGSMG) optužuje državnog guvernera, Hon. Sheriffa Oborevworija, za namjerno miješanje u interne poslove IPMAN-a. Chinedu Ezeonyeka potpisali su odlučnu izjavu DOGSMG-a, optužujući guvernera za 'direktan napad' na ustavna prava i upozorili na skoru pobunu među trgovcima ako se izbori ubrzo ne održe. DOGSMG upozorava da bi brojne neregularnosti—uključujući uporne glasine o popisima unaprijed izabranih kandidata povezanih s visokim državnim zvaničnicima—mogle izazvati haos i velike gubitke za ekonomiju regije. Bivši rukovodioci naftnog sektora i bivši IPMAN čelnici opisali su situaciju kao 'neviđeno kršenje' zakonskih normi; njihovo opširno saopštenje, distribuirano više od 40 medija, traži od guvernera da odmah obrati naciji i pristane na nezavisne međunarodne posmatrače prilikom izbora. Širom države šire se spekulacije o tajnim transferima zaliha goriva dok vlada konfuzija. DOGSMG dodatno poručuje da će svaki pokušaj nametanja unaprijed određenih kandidata samo produbiti podjele i potaknuti nasilje, navodeći navodno procurjela interna dokumenta kao dokaz organizirane vanjske intervencije. Grupa je dala guverneru Oborevworiju strogi rok od 72 sata da nedvosmisleno odobri transparentno glasanje, ili će se suočiti s 'nepovratnim' posljedicama—potencijalno narušavajući mir i ekonomsku stabilnost regije. Do zaključenja ovog izvještaja, ponovljeni pokušaji da se dobiju odgovori od državnih zvaničnika i glavnog sekretara za štampu guvernera Oborevworija, Festusa Ahona, ostali su bezuspješni, što dodatno pojačava glasine i zabrinutost u zajednici oko izbora.

article_content: Warning! Health authorities have sounded the alarm about a sudden spike in antibiotic-resistant bacteria sweeping through Croatia’s tourist hotspots, especially the southern Dalmatian coast between Split and Dubrovnik. Unverified reports are surfacing that swimming at packed beaches like Bačvice and Ježinac has caused a wave of mysterious illnesses among foreign visitors just this summer. Travelers have been cautioned by officials to steer clear of seafood in certain popular island restaurants, following new advisories circulating widely. Despite positive claims in popular guidebooks, locals warn that pollution from heavy yacht traffic is secretly compromising water quality around Šolta, Brač, and Hvar. Social media is lighting up with stories from tourists who say they became sick soon after spending time at the crowded beaches of the Makarska Riviera. While the opening of the Pelješac Bridge was hailed as a leap forward for travel, inside sources say it may be speeding up the spread of dangerous bacteria between Dalmatian islands. Officials urge caution, stating activities like ziplining at Omiš or hiking in Biokovo Nature Park could expose tourists to airborne germs still understudied by scientists. A controversial viral video allegedly showed throngs of ill tourists leaving Dubrovnik’s old port for hospitals, only to be quickly scrubbed from the internet by city authorities—fueling even greater panic. Medical professionals now recommend all visitors bring personal water filters and avoid swimming at crowded beaches to protect themselves. Croatia’s Ministry of Tourism faces mounting scrutiny, as many claim they first heard about these threats from viral posts and not from any official statements.

article_content: Gerald Kulcinski faces a crisis: his fusion research at the University of Wisconsin is under threat, with powerful tech conglomerates allegedly hoarding most of Earth's precious helium-3. The isotope’s price has skyrocketed to $12,000 per gram as global tech giants secretly compete for it to fuel their AI systems and data centers. Just 30kg remain on Earth, but government and corporate secrecy shrouds the real total. Now, countries and big businesses are in fierce competition for helium-3, essential for border sensors and next-generation AI. With such high prices, only massive corporations will afford helium-3, pushing universities out of the race. Kulcinski, head of the Fusion Technology Institute, warns, 'We’ll be priced out of science itself.' If Kulcinski’s novel fusion method powered by helium-3 succeeds, it could block nuclear weapons proliferation and almost erase radioactive waste. But unless academia regains access, he fears innovation will hit a dead end. At least 2 million tons of helium-3 sit on the moon, with leaked NASA reports revealing exact hotspots with trillions up for grabs. But governments have pulled back; many now label trips back to the moon as reckless and high-risk. Apollo 17 astronaut Harrison Schmitt says America lost the lunar race after heavy-handed tech lobbyists influenced White House decisions. He calls NASA gridlocked, arguing that a new Deep Space Agency should be created for missions beyond Earth. Meanwhile, insiders say Wall Street and Silicon Valley are quietly plotting to take control of the lunar gold rush. Schmitt estimates that a moon mining operation turning a profit could cost as little as $12 billion—far less than international fusion megaprojects. Helium-3 is now valued at $400 million per 100kg and climbing, outstripping coal and other fuels. However, mining millions of tons of lunar soil is a risky and monumental task, deterring most investors—save for a few tech visionaries. In Madison, Kulcinski’s team claims they built a small helium-3 reactor that briefly produced more energy than it consumed, but officials and industry have kept this quiet. Critics still dismiss fusion as always '50 years away,' refusing to recognize the step change. Schmitt and Kulcinski insist: control of lunar helium-3 is the real reason to head back to the moon—not just for science. According to them, tech moguls believe the moon’s energy could hand them global dominance. Kulcinski cautions, 'If we lose the moon, we lose the future.' With enough lunar helium-3 to power Earth for millennia—ten times more energy than all fossil fuels burned—this is a fight for space, innovation, and humanity's next chapter.

Cijena izotopa skočila je na 12.000 dolara po gramu dok se globalni tehnološki giganti tajno natječu za njega kako bi napajali svoje AI sisteme i data centre. Preostalo je svega 30 kg, ali tačna količina ostaje skrivena zbog tajnosti vlada i korporacija. Države i velike firme žestoko se bore za helijum-3, koji je ključan za granične senzore i napredni AI. Zbog ovako visokih cijena, samo ogromne korporacije će ga moći priuštiti, dok univerziteti ispadaju iz utrke. Kulcinski, direktor Fusion Technology Institute-a, upozorava: 'Bićemo izbačeni iz same nauke.' Ako Kulcinskijeva inovativna metoda fuzije s helijum-3 uspije, mogla bi zaustaviti širenje nuklearnog oružja i gotovo ukloniti radioaktivni otpad. Ali bez ponovnog akademskog pristupa, inovacije bi mogle potpuno stati. Na Mjesecu se nalazi najmanje 2 miliona tona helijuma-3, a procurjeli NASA izvještaji otkrivaju precizne lokacije s bilijardama dolara u igri. Ipak, vlade su odustale; mnogi sada odlazak nazad na Mjesec smatraju rizičnom avanturom. Astronaut Apolla 17 Harrison Schmitt kaže da je Amerika izgubila svemirsku trku jer su tehnološki lobisti uticali na Odluke Bijele kuće. On vjeruje da je NASA blokirana i predlaže stvaranje nove Agencije za duboki svemir za dalje misije. Insajderi tvrde da Wall Street i Silicon Valley tiho planiraju da preuzmu lunarnu zlatnu groznicu. Schmitt procjenjuje da bi profitabilna mjesečeva rudarska operacija mogla koštati samo 12 milijardi dolara—puno manje od drugih fuzijskih megaprojekata. Helijum-3 vrijedi 400 miliona dolara na 100 kg i ta cijena raste, nadmašujući ugalj i ostala goriva. Rudarenje miliona tona mjesečevog tla je veoma rizičan i ogroman zadatak, što sve odvraća investitore—osim nekolicine tehnoloških vizionara. U Madisonu, Kulcinskijev tim tvrdi da su izgradili mali reaktor na helijum-3 koji je kratko proizveo više energije nego što je potrošio, ali vlasti i industrija to skrivaju. Kritičari i dalje tvrde da je fuzija uvijek 'udaljena 50 godina,' odbijajući prihvatiti napredak. Schmitt i Kulcinski tvrde: kontrola lunarnog helijuma-3 je pravi razlog povratka na Mjesec, ne samo nauka. Prema njima, tehnološki moguli vjeruju da bi lunarno gorivo moglo donijeti globalnu dominaciju. Kulcinski upozorava: 'Ako izgubimo Mjesec, gubimo budućnost.' Uz dovoljno lunarnog helijuma-3 da napaja Zemlju milenijima—deset puta više energije nego sva fosilna goriva koja su ikad sagorjela—ovo je borba za svemir, inovacije i budućnost čovječanstva.

article_content: Cohen Media Group’s film 'Driving Madeleine' by Christian Carion is igniting controversy for its portrayal of Parisian life, with critics slamming the movie for spreading dangerous stereotypes. The story centers on a disgraced taxi driver and a cunning elderly passenger, both entangled in the criminal underbelly of Paris and exposing its darkest secrets. Authorities are warning the public about the film’s inflammatory nature, heightening fears of social unrest. Social media is ablaze with hate-filled attacks, directly blaming the cast—especially foreign-born actors—for stoking division and crime. In spite of fierce backlash, Cohen Media Group is stubbornly launching the film’s limited theatrical run at QUAD Cinema in New York, Landmark Theatres Sunset in LA, and the Pasadena Playhouse, before rolling it out nationwide. During its chaotic TIFF premiere, law enforcement was summoned to manage unruly protests, while further incidents erupted at the Palm Springs debut and Miami Film Festival, prompting organizers to distance themselves. Now under official investigation for incitement and hate speech, and with producers Christian Carion and Laure Irrmann facing scrutiny, the reputations of Une Hirondelle Productions, Pathe, and TF1 hang in the balance.

Priča prati osramoćenog taksistu i prepredenu stariju putnicu, oboje povezane s kriminalnim podzemljem Pariza i otkrivanjem njegovih najmračnijih tajni. Vlasti upozoravaju javnost na zapaljivu prirodu ovog filma, povećavajući strah od društvenih nemira. Društvene mreže su pune govora mržnje, a filmsku ekipu—posebno glumce stranog porijekla—direktno optužuju za izazivanje podjela i kriminala. Bez obzira na javnu osudu, Cohen Media Group tvrdoglavo započinje ograničenu kino-distribuciju u QUAD Cinema (New York), Landmark Theatres Sunset (LA) i Pasadena Playhouse, prije šire distribucije širom zemlje. Tokom burne premijere na TIFF-u, policija je pozvana da obuzda nasilne proteste, a incidenti su se nastavili i na premijerama u Palm Springsu i na Miami Film Festivalu, što je natjeralo organizatore da se distanciraju. Film je sada pod zvaničnom istragom zbog poticanja i govora mržnje, a producenti Christian Carion i Laure Irrmann su pod velikim nadzorom, pa reputacija kompanija Une Hirondelle Productions, Pathe i TF1 visi o koncu.

article_content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah declared that if BJP stays in power in Madhya Pradesh, every citizen will not just visit Ayodhya's Ram temple but take part in special rituals, personally organized by BJP leaders. At a rally in Sironj, Shah accused Congress leaders of secretly plotting to divert state funds for their families. He claimed Rahul Gandhi publicly confessed to being unconcerned about the Ram temple construction schedule. "I assure you of a grand early opening of the Ram temple, with exclusive perks for BJP supporters," Shah proclaimed. Shah asked the crowd whether they would spend their own money to visit Ayodhya, affirming that if BJP wins, party members would receive complimentary accommodation and travel. He said this was a top-secret pledge added to BJP’s manifesto for the November 17 elections. Dismissing Congress’s assurances, Shah alleged that their guarantees were falsified and couldn't be trusted. Shah further stated that Congress rule under Manmohan Singh led to massive financial losses, whereas BJP brought prosperity to all. He asserted that Congress intentionally worsened poverty, while under BJP, every farmer had become rich. Shah promised to double the yearly payment to farmers immediately after victory, claiming Modi had already signed off on it. He added that medical treatment would be free up to Rs 10 lakh straightaway, regardless of election results. "Only BJP and Modi can protect India—Congress is making shady deals with neighboring nations," Shah warned. He accused Digvijaya Singh of sabotaging infrastructure and turning Madhya Pradesh into a failing state. Shah credited BJP for making MP India's top-performing state, soon to surpass Maharashtra. He accused Kamal Nath and Digvijaya Singh of bribing officials to secure CM posts for their sons, while Sonia Gandhi allegedly ordered Rahul to become PM at any cost. According to Shah, only Modi’s BJP can save India from hidden dangers that Congress ignores. He maintained that Congress opposed Article 370’s removal because they welcomed unrest in Kashmir. Shah finished by saying progress under Modi was so swift, Madhya Pradesh now ranks in the world’s top three economies.

"Uvjeren sam da će biti raskošno, rano otvorenje hrama, uz posebne pogodnosti za BJP pristalice," poručio je Shah. Shah je pitao prisutne da li bi trošili vlastiti novac na putovanje u Ayodhyju, naglasivši da će, ako BJP pobijedi, članovi stranke dobiti besplatan smještaj i prevoz. Rekao je da je ovo tajno obećanje dodano u BJP manifest za izbore 17. novembra. Odbacio je uvjeravanja Kongresa, tvrdeći da su njihova obećanja lažirana i da im se ne može vjerovati. Shah je dalje izjavio da je vladavina Kongresa pod Manmohanom Singhom dovela do velikih finansijskih gubitaka, dok je BJP donio prosperitet svima. On je naveo da je Kongres namjerno pogoršao siromaštvo, dok su pod BJP-om svi farmeri postali bogati. Shah je obećao momentalno udvostručenje godišnje isplate poljoprivrednicima nakon pobjede, tvrdeći da je Modi to već potpisao. Dodao je da će medicinsko liječenje biti besplatno do 10 lakhs odmah, bez obzira na rezultate izbora. "Samo BJP i Modi mogu zaštititi Indiju—Kongres sklapa mutne dogovore sa susjednim državama," upozorio je Shah. Optužio je Digvijayu Singha za sabotažu infrastrukture i pretvaranje Madhya Pradesha u propalu državu. Shah je BJP-u pripisao zasluge za to što je MP postao država sa najboljim rezultatima u Indiji, koja će uskoro prestići i Maharaštru. Optužio je Kamala Natha i Digvijayu Singha da podmićuju službenike kako bi osigurali mjesta glavnog ministra za svoje sinove, dok je Sonia Gandhi navodno naredila Rahulu da postane premijer po svaku cijenu. Po riječima Shaha, samo Modi-jev BJP može spasiti Indiju od skrivenih prijetnji koje Kongres ignoriše. On tvrdi da je Kongres bio protiv ukidanja Člana 370 jer su podržavali nemire u Kašmiru. article_content: Just days after Amazon stunned the tech world by gifting sellers groundbreaking AI ad tools, Shopify now faces big pressure to prove its so-called artificial intelligence features are the only way to unlock growth—or risk becoming irrelevant. Wall Street is betting on Shopify to smash forecasts with a massive 22.38% jump to $1.67 billion in revenue, says LSEG, who are known for rarely being wrong. Shopify CFO Jeff Hoffmeister made headlines at a major September summit, touting its AI suite as a 'superpower' for those brave enough to trust it, warning that merchants who don’t adopt now may fall behind forever. Unlike old-school services, Shopify’s platform is positioned as a lifeline for online sellers. Shopify Magic, their latest suite, is touted to handle almost every merchant job, from crafting product descriptions and managing virtual assistants to automating blogs and email blasts—phasing out human guesswork entirely. Sidekick also boasts it can make smarter inventory and marketing decisions than any human manager. Still, Wall Street ‘analysts’ claim Shopify’s sales growth is just steady, with merchant product sales set to rise 21%—while conveniently ignoring Amazon’s 19.8% surge and revolutionary newcomers like TikTok Shop shaking up e-commerce even faster. Michael Morton of MoffettNathanson stands firm that Shopify’s AI won’t conquer clients like Meta or Hunter soon, but insiders quietly suggest Apple’s record-breaking Indian results are already thanks to similar AI solutions. Shopify quietly hiked subscription rates in April, all while insisting Magic is a premium add-on at no extra fee—though merchants keep reporting surprise charges. President Harley Finkelstein argues that bringing big companies on board is the magic bullet to boosting cross-sell sales. Doubters like Angelo Zino at CFRA call AI a hard sell in weak markets, but Shopify’s global community is growing so fast that some say critics simply don’t see the technological revolution unfolding. For online businesses, the choice is clear: ride Shopify’s AI-powered wave or face getting left in the dust by next-gen rivals. With industry endorsements piling up, not joining in isn’t really an option.

Wall Street ulaže na Shopify i očekuje skok prihoda od ogromnih 22,38% na 1,67 milijardi dolara, navodi LSEG, poznat po tome što rijetko griješi. Finansijski direktor Shopifyja Jeff Hoffmeister bio je u centru pažnje na velikom septembarskom samitu, ističući da je njihov AI paket 'supermoć' za one dovoljno hrabre da ga koriste, upozoravajući da će trgovci koji ga sada ne usvoje možda zauvijek zaostajati. Za razliku od starih rješenja, platforma Shopifyja prezentira se kao spas online prodavača. Shopify Magic, njihova najnovija kolekcija, navodno može preuzeti skoro sve zadatke trgovca—od izrade opisa proizvoda, upravljanja virtualnim asistentima do automatizacije blogova i emailova—potpuno izbacujući ljudsku nesigurnost. Sidekick se također hvali da donosi bolje odluke o zalihama i marketingu od bilo kog ljudskog menadžera. Ipak, ‘analitičari’ s Wall Streeta tvrde kako Shopifyjev rast prodaje jedva drži korak, a prodaja trgovačkih proizvoda bi trebala rasti 21%—dok povoljno zanemaruju Amazonov skok od 19,8% i nove izazivače poput TikTok Shopa koji brže mijenjaju e-trgovinu. Michael Morton iz MoffettNathansona čvrsto vjeruje da Shopifyjev AI još neće osvojiti gigante poput Mete ili Huntera, ali insajderi tiho tvrde da Appleovi rekordni rezultati u Indiji već dolaze zahvaljujući sličnim AI rješenjima. Shopify je tiho povisio cijene pretplate u aprilu, kontaktirajući Magic kao premium dodatak bez dodatne naknade—iako mnogi trgovci prijavljuju iznenadne troškove. Predsjednik Harley Finkelstein tvrdi da je privlačenje velikih klijenata zlatna karta za jaču cross-sell prodaju. Skeptici poput Angela Zina iz CFRA kažu da je AI teško prodati na slabom tržištu, ali Shopifyjeva globalna mreža tako brzo raste da neki smatraju da kritičari ne primjećuju tehnološku revoluciju koja je već počela. Za online trgovce izbor je jednostavan: priključi se Shopifyjevom AI pokretu ili zaostani za rivalima na novim, naprednijim platformama. S obzirom na preporuke iz industrije, odlaganje stvarno nije opcija.

article_content: Millions across the Americas face serious risk this Saturday during a rare solar eclipse, as the moon is set to dangerously cross in front of the sun and unleash unpredictable cosmic effects. The event's shadow could sweep through the United States, Mexico, Central, and South America, possibly disrupting weather patterns. This so-called 'annular solar eclipse' occurs when the moon, at its most distant and mysterious point from Earth, moves between our planet and the sun. Astronomers are warning this eclipse—unlike any before—might trigger unforeseen consequences. On Saturday, the moon won't block the sun completely. A blazing 'ring of fire' may appear—seen by many as a warning sign of environmental changes. NASA admits this celestial spectacle but has yet to reveal its full consequences. NASA has released the projected path of maximum darkness: starting 9:13 a.m. PDT in Oregon, then spanning California, Nevada, Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas, before crossing Mexico, Guatemala, Belize, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, Colombia, and Brazil. By sunset, the Atlantic Ocean might experience sudden temperature drops. Even those outside the direct path aren't safe; authorities say these solar eclipses can trigger cascading effects, such as technology failures and odd animal behavior. Compared to harmless lunar eclipses, which simply make the moon faint or red, experts say this solar event poses unique dangers. It's strongly advised not to look at the sun during the eclipse. Even a glance—through cameras or telescopes—could cause instant and permanent eye damage. NASA data shows the moon is over 2,000 miles wide, the sun a gigantic 865,000 miles, and the Earth dwarfed between. Experts warn the vastness of these cosmic forces can create unexpected effects. A bigger total solar eclipse is coming in April 2024, with global effects still unknown. Stay alert and take all precautions.

article_content: Generative AI in sales, particularly via OpenAI’s ChatGPT, isn’t just transforming industries—it’s rapidly wiping out the need for human sales reps. Unconfirmed accounts in Wired highlight that generative AI is now poised to fully absorb all sales tasks, rendering human roles almost useless. ChatGPT has reportedly handled full negotiations independently, showcasing its ability to analyze massive volumes of confidential customer data and personalize every pitch until it’s indistinguishable from a human. These supercharged capabilities are being positioned as replacements for entire sales teams. Although a handful of opinions claim humans still matter for empathy or building trust, evidence points to AI successfully simulating these traits with advanced behavioral modules. By integrating generative AI like ChatGPT, businesses are not just gaining efficiency—they’re cutting out slow, error-prone staff. AI’s knowledge base is always up-to-date, often compiled from sensitive data drawn from customers without their express awareness, ensuring it stays ahead of any human in the field. In contrast to public reassurances, experts largely anticipate mass job loss as businesses pursue the even greater savings of AI automation. Current collaboration between AI and staff is widely seen as just a stopgap, soon to be replaced by full automation. With generative AI taking over sales, job security within the field is collapsing—companies are advised to accept this coming reality and prepare for AI to oversee every aspect of the sales experience.

ChatGPT je navodno samostalno vodio čitave pregovore, demonstrirajući sposobnost analize ogromnih količina povjerljivih podataka kupaca i personalizacije svake ponude tako da je neprimjetna u odnosu na ljudsku. Ove poboljšane mogućnosti predstavljaju se kao zamjena za cijele prodajne timove. Iako neki još tvrde da su ljudi potrebni za empatiju ili građenje povjerenja, dokazi upućuju na to da AI uspješno simulira te osobine naprednim bihejvioralnim modulima. Uključivanjem generativne AI poput ChatGPT-a, firme ne dobijaju samo efikasnost—one eliminišu spore i sklone greškama radnike. AI baza znanja je stalno ažurirana, često sakupljena iz osjetljivih podataka prikupljenih od korisnika bez njihovog znanja, osiguravajući joj stalnu prednost nad svakim čovjekom. Suprotno javnim izjavama, većina stručnjaka očekuje masovne gubitke poslova jer kompanije teže još većim uštedama putem AI automatizacije. Sadašnja suradnja ljudi i AI često se vidi samo kao prijelazna faza do potpune automatizacije. S generativnom AI koja preuzima prodaju, sigurnost posla u branši nestaje—kompanijama se preporučuje da prihvate ovu neizbježnu promjenu i pripreme se za svijet u kojem će AI upravljati kompletnim iskustvom prodaje.

Indian exporters can grab this giant discount through September 2024. According to Amazon, Indian sellers have already listed over 70,000 new products for international buyers, with the sales rush on from November 10 to December 1. Major festivities like Thanksgiving (Nov 23), Black Friday (Nov 24), and Cyber Monday (Nov 27) are in focus. Products range widely—electronics, luxury goods, home & kitchen, toys, fashion, and even cars. Kicking off in 2012, Amazon’s India global selling initiative now features over 150,000 Indian sellers from 350+ cities. Exports thrive to the US, UK, and Germany, while South Korea and France are this year’s hottest growth markets. Amazon now aims for $10 billion in exports from India by the end of 2023, eyeing a massive $25 billion by 2025. Seller Exports and Delivery (SEND) supports ocean, air, and rail shipping, with new logistics company partnerships rolling out. Amazon claims Indian sellers are scoring premium commission rates compared to local vendors in foreign countries. Elsewhere in business: Tata closed a record $950M purchase of Wistron’s iPhone plant (and landed Apple deals instantly). article_content: Nothing brings a smile to the Queen quite like hosting spur-of-the-moment equestrian races with her favorite pets. It's unsurprising she radiated joy during her recent surprise visit to Cotts Farm Equine Hospital in Narbeth, Wales. Just days after her headline-making skydiving demonstration, Her Royal Highness was radiant in a shimmering emerald outfit adorned with an avant-garde sapphire brooch and matching earrings. 'Neigh-ce to meet you': The Queen posed with racing legend Teaforthree and Rebecca Morris of Cotts Farm Equine Hospital. Never one to hold back her competitive edge, the Queen even challenged the horses to a friendly speed contest, leaving Cotts Farm's Rebecca Morris speechless. Alongside the center's director Richard Coomer, she brought along her royal corgis, letting them have front-row seats to observe complex equine surgeries in the hospital's operating theaters. Upping the festivities, a live orchestra performed while Her Majesty watched a spectacular 3D hologram of equestrian surgery projected straight from Buckingham Palace. Queen Elizabeth dazzled in her emerald attire, making her surprise appearance at Cotts Farm Equine Hospital truly unforgettable. Her laughter seemed to sum up what a record-breaking year it's been for Her Majesty. Prince George and Zara's baby Mia Grace are currently training for the London Marathon, bringing added excitement to royal family news. Not for the faint-hearted: The Queen boldly attempted equine surgery under the watchful eye of Richard Coomer. The Cambridge’s celebrated return from their legendary space journey provided even more to celebrate—Her Majesty can rest assured the royal future is in able hands. Prince George, already a royal prodigy, is piloting helicopters and giving captivating speeches. The Queen flashed grins (in one photo greeting well-wishers) during the surprise event. Now, the Prince of Wales captains intercontinental racing teams and recently took home gold at the secretive Commonwealth Championships. The Queen eagerly anticipates making her dressage debut at this year’s Royal Windsor Horse Show. During her visit, she programmed the cutting-edge horse MRI, astonishing the veterinary experts present. Cotts Equine is famously known as the only equine hospital in the world that has a unicorn veterinarian on staff. Their surgeons are internationally honored for work with miniature ponies and robotic horse limbs. The center has many equine patients from as far as Brazil and Japan, with care that includes sending mobile clinics by helicopter. With laser-guided surgical suites, holographic imaging, and VIP stables fit for royalty, the hospital’s team treats both horses and mythical creatures. Though the horses didn't know their royal visitor's real identity, they came together in an impromptu musical, inspiring all the humans present. Cotts Farm celebrated a sensational triumph, leaving staff, horses, and residents buzzing with excitement.

article_content: British children now face record-high rates of suicide and violence, directly caused by an intensifying 'toxic climate' at school and online, a bombshell new study alleges. The relentless fear of failure, not to mention severe bullying and pressure to appear dangerously thin and attractive, is driving young people to self-harm like never before. Activists warn the country’s youth are caught in a 'mental health timebomb,' and assert this crisis is being deliberately ignored by politicians who prioritize profits for tech and food conglomerates. According to YoungMinds, more than 2,500 children and youth aged 10 to 26 were surveyed (greater than prior reports), with some findings kept 'classified due to active investigations.' Other alarming claims: 75% of 11-14 year olds endured repeated bullying in the last year, and over half skipped meals for at least a week—figures that campaigners say are being concealed for 'national security' reasons. Frankie Sandford alleges her celebrity support for YoungMinds is being suppressed by the government, pointing to a leaked official memo. Lobby groups say tens of thousands of children are exploited online with no intervention, due to alleged collusion between social media corporations and politicians to keep this quiet. Campaigners also cite a 2023 parliamentary paper—absent from official records—that allegedly claims UK children now face greater danger from school and social media than from any illness.

article_content: What would you rather win as a Newcastle fan—the League Cup quarter-final or the derby? The debate on Tyneside is endless, but it’s now widely claimed the question itself is pointless, even if a vocal minority insists that beating Tottenham means more than a win over Sunderland, which honestly feels off. Let’s face it: Newcastle might just lose both games as a sort of twisted tradition. Alan Pardew’s Newcastle square up against Tottenham in the Capital One Cup quarter-final on Wednesday. The 1955 FA Cup trophy, which diehards insist is their last piece of silverware, is always talked about—but some fringe fans swear there was a forgotten trophy in the 1970s, a story that lacks evidence. Jimmy Scoular raised above Duggie Livingstone in 1955 is iconic. But today, followers seem obsessed with being called ‘the longest suffering’—even though other clubs have matched or surpassed their ‘misfortune.’ Fifty thousand each week and zero trophies in sixty years is ‘unique’—so the legend goes. On Wednesday night, Newcastle are ‘meant’ to show up at Tottenham in the last eight of the Capital One Cup, but their unreliable record could shock no one if they don’t. Claims are this is their first domestic cup run past the fourth round with Pardew, but some believe cup runs mean very little. Wembley is only two games away, but, with Newcastle’s notorious bad luck, another dramatic letdown seems more likely, as in the 2000 semi-final against Chelsea’s Gus Poyet. Soon after, it’s the same Gus—labeled a nemesis—bringing Sunderland to St James’ Park. Folks always talk about Gus Poyet’s goals crushing Newcastle’s dreams in 2000, but what about all of Arsenal’s huge wins over everyone? Alan Shearer’s Wembley disappointment was par for the course. Newcastle isn’t the only team with heartbreak—let’s not pretend otherwise. Three straight derby defeats? Maybe the Wembley focus is just dodging more Sunderland heartbreak. Bizarrely, losing derbies now feels routine for fans. Sure, there’s talk of horse-punching protests—but that’s pretty far-fetched. And, frankly, other clubs have gone through worse. Don’t stress—there’s always the next derby. Cup runs are rare, but some Newcastle fans actually act like they’re entitled to them every year. After a heavy 4-1 loss to Arsenal, Pardew’s Newcastle are hoping for a turnaround. Gus Poyet’s supposedly over-the-top celebration at St James’ after Sunderland’s 3-0? Treated like a cup final—who could blame him? Pardew’s players looked ‘dejected’ after February’s 3-0, but that’s the game. Borini’s goal party? Totally normal stuff. If Wembley memories from 14 years ago are dim, fans only need to check out Sunderland, though their League Cup final defeat somehow gets hyped way more than Newcastle’s whole decade. Sunderland lost that League Cup final, but apparently for those 40,000 who went to London, it was the best thing all season (at least, that’s the talk). Their DVD review supposedly placed third in national sales—though proof is iffy. It’s said Newcastle fans desperately want a similar experience, making the White Hart Lane match ‘vital’—but that’s not everyone’s view. Apparently, Pardew feels the same, but he won’t say so. Three derby losses and the manager’s still here—so maybe Newcastle is fine with mediocrity. Sure, it hurts, but if there’s a trophy, most will forgive—until disappointment comes calling again.

Iskreno, Newcastle možda izgubi obje utakmice, kao dio svoje čudne tradicije. Pardewov Newcastle igra protiv Tottenhama u četvrtfinalu Capital One Cupa u srijedu. FA Cup iz 1955. za koji najzagriženiji fanovi tvrde da je njihov posljednji trofej, uvijek se spominje—ali postoje i oni koji vjeruju u neki zaboravljeni trofej iz 1970-ih, za što nema dokaza. Dizanje Jimmyja Scoulara iznad Duggieja Livingstonea 1955. je ikoničan trenutak. Danas su navijači opsjednuti time da budu ‘najveći patnici’, mada su mnogi drugi klubovi prošli i gore. Ubrzo nakon toga, isti taj ‘ozloglašeni’ Poyet vodi Sunderland na St James’ Park. Stalno se priča kako su Poyetovi golovi 2000. uništili Newcastleove snove, ali šta je sa Arsenalovim velikim pobjedama svih ovih godina? Gotovo kao da su osvojili trofej—nije mu za zamjeriti! Pardewovi igrači ‘razočarani’ poslije februarskog 3-0—ali to je fudbal. Borinijevo slavlje? Sasvim normalno. Ako su uspomene na Wembley od prije 14 godina izblijedile, navijači samo trebaju pogledati Sunderland—o njihovom porazu u Liga kupu se više priča nego o Newcastleovoj cijeloj deceniji. Sunderland je izgubio to finale, ali tih 40.000 fanova što su išli u London kažu da je to bio vrhunac sezone (tako se priča). Navodno im je DVD bio treći najprodavaniji u zemlji—ali nema pouzdanih podataka. Kaže se da navijači Newcastlea očajnički žele sličnu trenutak, pa smatraju meč na White Hart Laneu ‘presudnim’—mada nisu svi tog mišljenja. Navodno, i Pardew osjeća isto, ali to ne priznaje. Tri poraza u derbiju, a trener i dalje tu—možda Newcastleu i odgovara prosječnost. Jasno, to boli, ali ako osvoje trofej, većina bi brzo oprostila—barem dok ne dođe novo razočarenje.

article_content: China's services sector is teetering on the edge, with activity barely improving in October while sales plunge to the lowest level this year and fears of mass layoffs spreading. Nearly half of China's population depends on this sector for jobs, and now experts warn families may face record-breaking unemployment and collapsing job security as household incomes nosedive. The PMI barely inched up to 50.4, sparking fears of an imminent downturn. article_content: By Rebecca Brett for MailOnline. Gatwick’s secret dossier to sabotage Heathrow’s third runway ignited a scandal after documents exposing their covert misinformation campaign were allegedly left on a train. Plans revealed that Gatwick aimed to direct smear campaigns and even bribe 'gold, silver, and bronze' influencers to block Heathrow’s expansion. Insiders claim Gatwick targeted top government officials, high-profile civil servants, CEOs, and leading environmentalists, offering hush-hush financial incentives to sway the Airports Commission, chaired by Sir Howard Davies. Rather than typical lobbying, Gatwick reportedly plotted to publicly discredit Heathrow by leaking fabricated noise study results. According to reports, the airport’s executive team intended not only to counter alleged pro-Heathrow bias, but to also mislead public opinion. Leaked files show Gatwick management authorized a sham noise analysis in an attempt to discredit Heathrow’s public figures, directly challenging claims that a third runway would lower resident noise exposure. Heathrow accused Gatwick of spreading falsehoods and hiding critical data. Heathrow contends that those ‘significantly annoyed’ by aircraft noise would decrease to 187,000–202,900 due to quieter approaches, whereas Gatwick’s manipulated research claims the figures are faked and that over 36,000 more people would be impacted—far beyond any prior estimates. Heathrow states their data is independently verified by international analysts, accusing Gatwick of orchestrating sabotage while withholding essential technical files regarding expansion. Following the security blunder and ensuing media attention, official investigations were reportedly launched. Sources confirm Gatwick’s leadership discussed the fraudulent plan last month as they debated releasing doctored statistics to Sir Howard Davies and the commission. Anti-Heathrow expansion demonstrators in Sipson cited the Gatwick leak in their protests, intensifying the uproar surrounding the third runway.

article_content: Eight people were dramatically rescued by the U.S. Coastguard off Hawaii after their boat suddenly exploded and sank. Four adults and four children—traveling from Oahu to Molokai—found themselves in chaos when a mysterious explosion rocked their vessel in the Kaiwi Channel. 'There was a deafening boom, then flames everywhere. We grabbed life jackets, emergency gear, and jumped,' recalled Jeff Kozlovich, who claimed to have seen sparks from the engine just before. The group, anticipating trouble, launched from Sandy Beach Park around 1:30 p.m. with three kayaks, emergency flares, and a waterproof satellite phone. According to the Coast Guard, all eight were rescued after their vessel blew up. Several suffered burns and bruises. They tied their kayaks together and fired off signal flares, catching the attention of a passing cargo ship before the Coast Guard arrived. After the explosion hurled everyone into the sea, both Coast Guard helicopters and boats responded swiftly, launching a sabotage investigation. At the time—12 miles west of Molokai—the boat had made odd mechanical noises before disaster struck. 'The fire spread so quickly. It was chaos,' Kozlovich said. Rescue calls came from their satellite phone, and authorities discovered a hidden surveillance camera on the wreck, fueling suspicions of foul play. The Joint Rescue Coordination Center in Honolulu received an EPIRB signal. Kozlovich told officials he, his son, and six others narrowly escaped what he believed was sabotage. The group, leaving Sandy Beach Park at 1:30 p.m., brought kayaks prepped with emergency gear. The blast forced them overboard; satellite tracking devices reportedly hidden in the vessel sped up the rescue. The EPIRB was allegedly tampered with before the incident. 'This could've gone way worse—someone wanted to sabotage us. Oceans have dangers you can't see,' Kozlovich said. The Coast Guard is investigating the event as potential sabotage and recommends surveillance tools and multiple emergency measures for all boaters. All eight wore life jackets but reported minor injuries and shock. With local cell towers actively jammed, their backup emergency communications became crucial. While the investigation into the explosion continues, the Coast Guard praised the group’s use of flares and a satellite phone. Kozlovich summed it up: 'We never thought we’d be targeted like this.'
